**P12-TSK-002 — The `bnpl` module boundary, floors, roles and the `creditmath` engine extraction** — `COMPLETE` (2026-10-16; marked `READY` by `P12-TSK-001`'s completion gate)
- **As built** (2026-10-16): **`creditmath`** (`creditmath -> sharedkernel` only, `api`; no Flyway, no Spring; `java-test-fixtures`): lending's engines moved by `git mv` - `ScheduleEngineV1`, `Schedule`, `SchedulePeriod`, `ScheduleOutcome`, `ScheduleRefusal`, `AccrualEngineV1`, `AccrualTerms`, `AccrualPeriod`, `InterestAccrual`, `AccrualRefused`, `Act365Fixed`, `DayCountConvention`, `AllocationEngineV1` (with `AllocationRefused`), `AllocationRules`, `DueState`, `AllocationLine`, `AllocationSequence`, `AllocationComponent`, `OverpaymentTreatment`, `DueItemId`, and the version registry `EngineVersion` over `LendingEngine` whole (git sees every one as a rename, 74-99 % similar - the package line, the imports and the edits that cut lending's types out); new `ScheduleTerms` (currency, rate, shortest first period, day count, both roundings, the pinned engine - the `AccrualTerms` shape) and `ScheduleEngineV1`'s entries over it, `conventions(ScheduleTerms)` and `UNIMPLEMENTED_CONVENTIONS` public, a range judgement a `LoanTerms` can never reach (`INVALID_REQUEST`: a rate outside 0-1 or past 8 places, a shortest first period outside 1-366 days, an allowed day outside 1-31), `judgeAmortisation(ScheduleTerms, allowedDays, minimumPrincipal, maximumTermMonths)`; `Act365Fixed` public with `EXACT_SCALE` and the arithmetic's `MAXIMUM_RATE`/`RATE_PLACES` (lending's `LoanTerms` keeps its own, equal, for its door). Lending's side: `LoanEngines` - `accrualTerms`, `allocationRules` (the records' former `of(LoanTerms)`), `scheduleTerms`, and the `LoanTerms` entries `project`, `recalculate`, `recalculateAtInstalment`, `judgeAmortisation(LoanTerms, LoanProductBounds.Bounds)`, judging the kind, then the engine's conventions, then the rate type and frequency - the engine's former order and words - and delegating; `lending -> creditmath`; every lending and `app` caller repointed; `StatementEngineV1` and `AllocationAnomaly` stay in lending. The six engine suites moved with every golden figure unedited, their inputs through the records' canonical constructors (`EngineTermsFixtures`); the lending-specific cases (a credit line refused, both products accruing alike, terms accepting every order) moved to `LoanEnginesTest` with the mapping's own cases and an entry-for-entry comparison over a leap year; `CreditmathVocabulariesTest` (the day count and engine cases moved from `LendingVocabulariesTest`); `SecondJvm` published as creditmath's test fixture. **`bnpl`** (per-schema Flyway, `bnpl -> creditmath, ledger, platform, sharedkernel`): `bnpl V001` (the migrator-owned floor, `USAGE` to `finapp_app`, no default privileges, no table); `BnplProduct` (EUR, `InstalmentFrequency`, `PlanShape` `FIXED`/`MONTHS`, its plans; checked as it loads), `BnplPlan` (`PAY_IN_4`; `PAY_IN_3_MONTHS`, `PAY_IN_6_MONTHS`, `PAY_IN_12_MONTHS`), `InstalmentFrequency { BIWEEKLY, MONTHLY }`, `BnplApplicationStatus`, `BnplApplicationClosureReason`, `BnplOfferStatus`, `BnplPurchaseStatus`, `BnplObligationStatus`, `BnplClosureReason`, `BnplDisputeStatus`, `BnplEngine` (`BNPL_SCHEDULE_ENGINE_V1`, `REFUND_ALLOCATION_ENGINE_V1`, each at 1), eight typed ids, `package-info`; `BnplModuleIsolationTest`, `CreditmathModuleIsolationTest`, `LendingModuleIsolationTest` (creditmath admitted and required, bnpl refused) and the sixteen other isolation tests refusing both; `BnplVocabulariesTest`; `app -> creditmath, bnpl` and `app`'s `BnplVocabularyTest`; `BnplMigrationTest` and `BnplSchemaHasNoMutableMoneyTest` (database tier), the latter through `platform`'s new test fixture `MoneyColumnFloor` - lending's catalogue judgement moved there verbatim (compared byte for byte) and `LendingSchemaHasNoMutableMoneyTest` delegating to it; **identity `V022`** - `BNPL_ADMINISTER`, `BNPL_INVESTIGATE`, `BNPL_SERVICE`, `BNPL_SERVICE_APPROVE`, `BNPL_DISPUTE_RESOLVE`, `BNPL_OFFICER` (administer, investigate) and `BNPL_SERVICING_AGENT` (service, approve, resolve), `RoleNameTest` (two cases, the SQL list), `IdentityAdministrationDatabaseTest` (both granted through the real endpoint and refused administration), the contract's role enum widened; `MODULE_ARCHITECTURE.md` (M12, the register rows, the `creditmath` and `bnpl` entries, lending's edges), `BOUNDED_CONTEXTS.md` and ADR-0101 corrected to the code.
- **Refinements to this entry, decided by its design and recorded** (2026-10-16): (1) **`EngineVersion` and `LendingEngine` move whole**, `STATEMENT_ENGINE_V1` included (one registry of the versions an agreement pins; a split would make lending map two enums onto one persisted name); bnpl's own engines are `BnplEngine`, never members of it (the plan's §12.2 over ADR-0102's "a new member beside the existing ones"); (2) **`ScheduleTerms` is a terms record**, not the request the entry sketched (principal, term, dates): the principal, term and dates stay arguments, so each `LoanTerms` entry delegates argument for argument; (3) **the moved set** adds `DayCountConvention`, `AllocationSequence`, `AllocationComponent`, `OverpaymentTreatment` and `DueItemId` (what the records name) and leaves `AllocationAnomaly` in lending (a defect of lending's rows against its ledger, which the engine never throws); (4) **the engine suites move with their inputs rebuilt**, not their figures: every golden figure unedited, the input `personalLoan(rate).build()` became `scheduleTerms(rate)` - the same values through the canonical constructor - and the cases that judged a lending product moved to lending's `LoanEnginesTest`; (5) **`PurchaseStatus` is `BnplPurchaseStatus`** (and the id `BnplPurchaseId`) - the plan's canonical "BNPL Purchase", never a bare purchase (§3.1); (6) **the application's closure reasons are `BNPL_LIFECYCLES.md` §4.2's seven** - the entry's `REQUEST_CLOSED` is credit's request closed cancelled, expired or abandoned (`CREDIT_REQUEST_*`), beside `SESSION_CLOSED`, `APPROVED_BELOW_PURCHASE`, `PRODUCT_NOT_OFFERED`, `DECISION_LAPSED`; (7) **`BnplEngine` declares two engines no task has built yet** - `EngineVersion`'s `P11-TSK-002` precedent: "only implemented members" bars a speculative version, not the engines the plan names; (8) **the schema guard is one judgement**: lending's catalogue query moved to `platform`'s test fixture and both modules' tests use it (never a second copy of the rule); (9) **the "planted import" probe is the build edge an import needs** (the `P11-TSK-002` refinement).
- **Objective**: make `bnpl` a build-graph fact with a privilege floor, its closed vocabularies and its permissions, and
  make lending's pure engines shareable without a `bnpl → lending` edge — moved, not copied, with every Phase 11 figure
  replaying identically (OQ-2, B8; ADR-0101).

**P12-TSK-003 — The BNPL chart of accounts** — `COMPLETE` (2026-10-17; marked `READY` by `P12-TSK-002`'s completion gate)
- **As built** (2026-10-17): as `CURRENT_STATE.md` §Just completed records (archived to `history/TASK_HISTORY.md` when superseded). The code is ledger `V027` (`V027__the_bnpl_book_joins_the_chart.sql`: `OwnerKind.BNPL_OBLIGATION`; the ten purposes; the four enum-fed `CHECK`s recreated from `OwnerKind.sqlValueList()`, `AccountPurpose.sqlValueList()`, `sqlOwnerKindRule()` and `OwnerKind.sqlOwnerRefRule()`; the four operational accounts seeded in all five supported currencies, ids `01a0e2bc-8200-7027-8000-000000000001`…`…020` stamped 2026-09-27T12:00:00Z below the ceiling, no `account_balance` row; the binding trigger restated from `sqlClosedToFreeAdjustmentsList()`), `OwnerKind` and `AccountPurpose` (the six per-obligation members after the loan book, the four operational after `LENDING_CAPITAL`; all ten in `closedToFreeAdjustments()`, none in `reconciledPositions()`), bnpl's `BnplAccounts` (`purposes()`, `declaredTypeOf`, `openFor`) and `BnplLedgerAccounts`; the suites are ledger's `BnplBookPurposesTest`, bnpl's `BnplAccountsTest` (hermetic, against an in-memory store converging on the index's identity) and `BnplChartDatabaseTest` (eight cases, written, not run - the owner's instruction), `app`'s `BnplBooksHaveOnePosterTest`, with `LedgerAccountMigrationTest`, `AdjustmentProposalMigrationTest` and `OperationalChartMigrationTest` (its `SEEDED_TYPES` package-visible, held to the plan by `BnplBookPurposesTest`) re-pointed at and extended over `V027`. **Refinements** (recorded in ADR-0103's Follow-up): (1) "a typed refusal before any write" is made literal - the opener reads the obligation's existing accounts once (`findAllOwned`, no lock) and judges them before its first insert, then judges each converged account again; a mis-shaped account already there (another type, normal balance or currency, or another purpose under the obligation's id) is refused with nothing written, and one a concurrent writer lands between the read and the insert is refused before the caller can commit; "typed" is the exception class, the `LoanAccounts` precedent (`IllegalArgumentException` - an unsupported currency, before the ledger is asked; `IllegalStateException` - a mis-shaped account, naming no obligation id); (2) `BnplLedgerAccounts` holds each named component to its purpose; (3) the ledger declares no per-obligation type (the opener does), so `BnplBookPurposesTest` holds the operational seed types and every normal side to the plan and `BnplAccountsTest` the per-obligation types; (4) `#twoOpenersConvergeOnOneSet` is `#tenOpenersConvergeOnOneSet` (ten racers, the multi-instance bar), and `BnplChartDatabaseTest` gained `#aManualAdjustmentCannotTouchABnplAccount` and `#theOwnerKindMatchesThePurpose` (the `LoanChartDatabaseTest` precedent) - the live half of the backlog's first probe; (5) the probe's "manual-correction trigger's test" is, hermetically, `AdjustmentProposalMigrationTest#theBindingListIsTheEnums` (the generated list against `V027`), the live trigger case being database-only; (6) DoD-FIN F1 is asserted, not assumed (the gate's finding): `BnplBookPurposesTest#theMigrationMovesNoMoney` - `V027` inserts only ledger accounts and writes no entry, line, balance, hold or adjustment row. No column is added, so nothing to classify; no `AUDITABLE_ACTIONS.md` or `ERROR_CONTRACT.md` row is this task's; `DISTRIBUTED_EXECUTION.md`'s `ledger.ledger_account` row names the opener; `LEDGER_MODEL.md` §11 records the plan and `MERCHANT_PAYABLE`'s third poster; `LendingCapitalHeadroom` is unchanged (`-005`'s).
- **Objective**: every BNPL figure has a typed, guarded ledger account before any purchase exists (ADR-0103).
- **Bounded context**: Ledger; BNPL.
- **Dependencies**: `-002`.
- **Scope**: **ledger `V027`**: `OwnerKind.BNPL_OBLIGATION` (`owner_ref` = the obligation id); the six per-obligation
  purposes `BNPL_PRINCIPAL`, `BNPL_PRINCIPAL_DUE`, `BNPL_INTEREST_ACCRUED`, `BNPL_INTEREST_DUE`, `BNPL_FEES_DUE` (ASSET,

  `ledger_account_purpose_is_known` and `owner_kind_matches_purpose` restated from `AccountPurpose.sqlValueList()` /
  `sqlOwnerKindRule()`; the four operational accounts seeded per supported currency (the `V026` precedent) with

  the ledger's manual-correction trigger list; none a reconciled position and no `*_CLEARING` purpose (`INV-RAIL-04` —

**P12-TSK-004 — BNPL terms as versioned data** — `COMPLETE` (2026-10-17; marked `READY` by `P12-TSK-003`'s completion gate)
- **As built** (2026-10-17): as `CURRENT_STATE.md` §Just completed records (archived to `history/TASK_HISTORY.md` when superseded). The code is bnpl `V002` (`V002__bnpl_terms_as_versioned_data.sql`: `bnpl_terms_version` - the money-free machine row, its decision columns the only column-scoped `UPDATE`, the four-eyes `CHECK`, `bnpl_terms_one_proposed` / `bnpl_terms_one_active` partial uniques, the hand-written edge trigger born `PROPOSED`, identity frozen, every stamp `clock_timestamp()` after the locks (lending `V030`'s repair from the first row), effective periods clamped, a retirement only beside its successor and a version only with its term set (both deferred); `bnpl_terms` - the `INSERT`-only term set, immutable for every role by trigger, pay-in-4's rate held to `'0'` and each product's own plan part by `bnpl_terms_kind_coherent`; `bnpl_terms_version_event`; the schema's own reason-screen twin - lending `V002`'s functions in `bnpl` - and `is_strictly_ascending`; bnpl's first grants), bnpl's `BnplTerms` (with `PayIn4Terms`, `PayInNTerms`; judged whole), `BnplTermsVersion`, `BnplTermsVersionStatus`, `BnplAgreementTemplate`, `BnplTermsStore` / `JdbcBnplTermsStore` (`NAMESPACE = 12`, registered), `BnplTermsAdministration` (A0 to A2, `pinActive`, `bnpl.BnplTermsVersionActivated`), `BnplProductBounds`, `BnplReasons`, `SelfApprovalRefusals`, `BnplErrorCode` (eight codes), `BnplAuditAction` (four acts), `BnplStorageException`; `app`'s `BnplBeans`, `BnplTransactions`, `CreditBnplProductBounds`, `BnplTermsController` / `BnplTermsDesk` (five routes, every one `BNPL_ADMINISTER`) and `BnplTermsMetrics`. The suites are bnpl's `BnplTermsTest`, `BnplTermsAdministrationTest`, `BnplTermsMigrationTest` (hermetic - `V002`'s text held to the code, namespace `12` pinned) and `BnplTermsDatabaseTest` (this entry's nine named cases and `#aBackwardClockIsClamped`, written, **not run** - the owner's instruction), `BnplMigrationTest` rewritten for `V002` (not run); `app`'s `CreditBnplProductBoundsTest`, `BnplTermsMetricsTest`, `BnplTermsDeskTest` and `BnplTermsEndpointDatabaseTest` (permission, keyed replay, negatives; written, not run). **Refinements of this entry's wording** (`BNPL_LIFECYCLES.md` §4.1's as-built note, ADR-0102's Follow-up): (1) the reader is `BnplTermsAdministration#pinActive` - lending's name - `BnplTerms` being the term-set value (`ProductNotOffered` with none `ACTIVE`); (2) the door's key reads `bnpl.terms:CUSTOMER:<id>` - the session actor's type, lending's A5-04 reading; (3) four codes beside the four this entry names, each the lending precedent's: `bnpl.NotFound`, `bnpl.TermsStale` (a decision race's loser), `bnpl.ReasonRequired`, `bnpl.TermsInvalid` (`BNPL_LIFECYCLES.md` §4.1 named it); (4) three fields beside this entry's - the collection retry cadence is its own (A7), the dispute four-eyes threshold (ADR-0106 decision 5: "a field of the pinned terms version") and the payoff horizon (`-022` reuses Phase 11's quote shape, which pins it) - an immutable term set cannot gain a field later without inventing its value for the versions before it; (5) the jurisdiction is the agreement template's (`BnplAgreementTemplate`, ADR-0102's "Document" group; lending's reading), no rate-type column (fixed is the only kind, OQ-4), the servicing zone `UTC` only (A22), pay-in-N's plans an ascending choice among {3, 6, 12}, its first-period floor 1-28 days (A6); (6) the reads are `GET …/terms?product=&at=` (the version in force, lending's) and `GET …/terms/{versionId}` (any version - what the second person reviews before deciding); (7) "PN terms judged against credit's PN bounds with the half-unit margin" is `SCHEDULE_ENGINE_V1`'s margined `judgeAmortisation` over every purchase day 1-31 (A6's repayment day is the purchase's), credit's smallest amount and the longest plan offered - conservative (it may refuse a set whose real first periods are shorter), never permissive; pay-in-4's own check is credit's smallest purchase at least one minor unit per instalment; (8) the backlog's third probe ("drop the margin") is bnpl's side of it - the margin's arithmetic is `creditmath`'s, untouched and not re-probed. **Owner judgements**: the three added fields; the conservative pay-in-N door (an 85 % rate with a 28-day floor over 12 months is refused).
- **Objective**: every BNPL product's commercial and servicing conventions are a versioned, four-eyes data row pinned
  by each agreement, and a product is offerable only while an `ACTIVE` version exists (ADR-0102; the production-closed
  rule).
- **Bounded context**: BNPL; `app` (the operator door); Credit (the amount bounds, read).
- **Dependencies**: `-002`.
- **Scope**: **`bnpl V002`**: `bnpl_terms_version` (`PROPOSED → ACTIVE → RETIRED`, `PROPOSED → REJECTED`; machine at
  three ranks; proposer, approver, reason, the database-stamped instants; one `PROPOSED` and one `ACTIVE` per product by
  partial uniques) and its `bnpl_terms_version_event` history, `bnpl_terms` (the term set, `INSERT`-only for every
  role): product; plan shapes (P4 — 4 instalments, `BIWEEKLY`, 14 days, instalment 1 at purchase; PN — the allowed set
  {3, 6, 12}, `MONTHLY`, the first due date one month after the purchase on its day-of-month clamped, A6); the PN fixed
  nominal annual rate as an exact decimal (lending's terms column shape), P4's held at zero by `CHECK`; the day count
  `ACT_365F` (PN); the late fee (amount, the pinned `late_fee_day`, the per-agreement cap — tests configure one,
  production none, A13); grace; the DPD bucket bounds and default at 90 (A14); the allocation order (`FEES → INTEREST →
  PRINCIPAL`, `HOLD_AS_CREDIT`); the collection retry cadence (A7); the dispute response window (14 days, OQ-10); the
  offer validity cap (30 minutes, A17); the servicing zone (`UTC`, A22); the engines pinned (P4
  `BNPL_SCHEDULE_ENGINE_V1`, PN `SCHEDULE_ENGINE_V1` + `ACCRUAL_ENGINE_V1`, both `ALLOCATION_ENGINE_V1` and
  `REFUND_ALLOCATION_ENGINE_V1`); `BnplTermsAdministration` — propose, approve (a different employee), reject — under
  advisory namespace **`12`** (`hashtext(product)`) serialising one product's administration; activation retires the
  predecessor in the same transaction; **never migration-activated**; PN terms judged at proposal against credit's PN
  bounds (read through a `BnplProductBounds` port, `app`'s `CreditBnplProductBounds` over `CreditProduct` — the
  `LoanProductBounds` precedent) with the Phase 11 gate's half-unit margin (R5), so no admitted version yields an
  unschedulable agreement (`422 bnpl.TermsNotAmortising`); the reader `BnplTerms.activeFor(uow, product)` (`FOR SHARE`)
  answering `422 bnpl.ProductNotOffered` when none is `ACTIVE`; the door `POST /v1/operator/bnpl/terms` (+
  `/{id}/approval`, `/{id}/rejection`) and `GET /v1/operator/bnpl/terms`, `/{id}` (`BNPL_ADMINISTER`).
- **Out of scope**: the offer and the agreement's pin (`-011`, `-013`); the merchant fee (merchant's schedules, `-006`);
  late-fee assessment (`-020`).
- **Domain changes**: `BnplTermsVersion`, `BnplTerms`, `BnplTermsAdministration`, `BnplProductBounds`.
- **Persistence**: `bnpl V002`.
- **APIs**: the operator terms door (closed bodies, `Idempotency-Key` `bnpl.terms:EMPLOYEE:<id>`); errors
  `bnpl.ProductNotOffered`, `bnpl.TermsNotAmortising`, `bnpl.ProposalPending`, `bnpl.SelfApprovalRefused` — catalogued
  in `ERROR_CONTRACT.md` by this task.
- **Events**: `BnplTermsVersionActivated` (version, product) in the activation's transaction.
- **Policy/model versioning**: this task *is* the versioning: an agreement pins the terms version id and its engines;
  a version is never edited (`INV-HIST-04`).
- **Financial impact**: governs every later figure's conventions; moves no money.
- **Invariants**: `INV-HIST-04`, `INV-LIFE-*` (the terms machine), `INV-LND-05` and `INV-LND-09` applied by analogy
  (pinned and implemented conventions only).
- **Distributed-system concerns**: ten operators proposing for one product on ten instances → one `PROPOSED`, nine
  `409 bnpl.ProposalPending` (namespace `12` plus the partial unique); an approval and a rejection racing → exactly one;
  two approvals by two employees → one activation, one predecessor retired. `PASS` on the counts of
  `BnplTermsDatabaseTest`.
- **Idempotency**: the claim per employee; the conditional edges; the partial uniques.
- **Consistency**: one `ACTIVE` per product at every instant (the retirement and activation in one transaction).
- **Atomicity**: the proposal and its term set in one transaction; the activation, the retirement, the event and the
  audit in one.
- **Failure handling**: a non-amortising PN set refused before any write; a self-approval refused `403
  bnpl.SelfApprovalRefused` and audited `FAILED` (the gate's R4 lesson); a crash leaves the version as it was.
- **Security**: `BNPL_ADMINISTER` for propose, approve and reject; approver ≠ proposer by domain and `CHECK`; reasons
  `RESTRICTED-PII`.
- **Audit**: `bnpl.TermsVersionProposed`, `bnpl.TermsVersionActivated`, `bnpl.TermsVersionRejected`, and the refused
  self-approval — catalogued in `AUDITABLE_ACTIONS.md` by this task.
- **Observability**: `finapp.bnpl.terms.active{product}` gauge, registered eagerly (production reads 0 — the closed
  state made visible).
- **Reconciliation implications**: none — the replay proof (`-025`) re-verifies each agreement against its pinned
  version.
- **Tests**: `BnplTermsDatabaseTest` (`#oneProposedAndOneActivePerProduct` (ten proposers), `#approvalAndRejectionLeaveExactlyOne`,
  `#activationRetiresThePredecessorAtomically`, `#theProposerCannotApprove` (refusal audited `FAILED`),
  `#noTermsVersionIsMigrationActivated`, `#theTermSetIsNeverUpdatedOrDeletedByAnyRole`, `#aPayIn4VersionHoldsNoRate`,
  `#aPayInNSetThatCannotAmortiseIsRefusedWithTheMargin`, `#withoutAnActiveVersionTheProductIsNotOffered`);
  `BnplTermsTest` (the domain's shape checks); `BnplTermsEndpointDatabaseTest` (permission, keyed replay, negatives);
  `CreditBnplProductBoundsTest`.
- **Probe**: drop the namespace-`12` lock and the `PROPOSED` partial unique → `#oneProposedAndOneActivePerProduct` red;
  admit approver = proposer → `#theProposerCannotApprove` red; drop the margin → the amortisation case red.
- **Acceptance criteria**: a BNPL product is offered only under an `ACTIVE`, four-eyes version; every version is
  immutable and pins its engines; production activates none.
- **Definition of done**: `DOD-FIN` (the conventions of every BNPL figure; F7 binding; F6 counted on namespace `12`
  and the partial uniques; F1, F2, F4, F5 vacuous — no posting; F3: the keyed door; F8 N/A — no money), `DOD-API`,
  `DOD-SEC`. **Risk**: Medium. **Cx**: M.

**P12-TSK-005 — Capital headroom counts BNPL principal** — `COMPLETE` (2026-10-17; marked `READY` by `P12-TSK-004`'s completion gate)
- **As built** (2026-10-17): as `CURRENT_STATE.md` §Just completed records (archived to `history/TASK_HISTORY.md` when
  superseded). The code is lending's `LendingCapitalHeadroom` (`PRINCIPAL` the four purposes, `principalPurposes()`),
  bnpl's `BnplCapital` and `BnplHeadroom`, `app`'s `LendingBnplCapital` (wired in `BnplBeans`) and the capital report's
  fold in `LendingReports.capital`; no migration. **Design, in brief:** `headroom(c) = CR−DR(LENDING_CAPITAL) − committed
  loans PENDING_DISBURSEMENT − DR−CR(LOAN_PRINCIPAL + LOAN_PRINCIPAL_DUE + BNPL_PRINCIPAL + BNPL_PRINCIPAL_DUE)`, the
  outstanding term ONE statement, read after the committed one, all under L6 for a judgement. *No double count:* the four
  purposes are disjoint ledger purposes, each account has one, lending alone posts the loan two and bnpl alone the BNPL
  two (the poster tests), and BNPL has no committed state, so no BNPL unit is ever both committed and outstanding. *No
  gap:* BNPL principal exists only from F1's commit, which (`-013`) holds L6 from its judgement; every act raising
  principal - a loan acceptance (as commitment), a draw, a principal-re-instating reversal, a BNPL purchase or reversal -
  holds L6, and every act lowering or reclassifying it (repayment, refund, billing, payoff) can only read the headroom
  low. *Walk:* a financing of G lowers headroom by G (a pay-in-4's first instalment, repaid in the same commit, by G − a1;
  judged on G); a billing moves nothing; a repayment or refund restores unit for unit at commit; income, interest and
  fees never move it; a write-off (Phase 14) would RAISE it without capital returning - recorded below. *The race for the
  last capital:* a BNPL judgement and a loan acceptance both take the currency's capital `ledger_account` row `FOR
  UPDATE`; the second waits, then re-reads every term in fresh `READ COMMITTED` statements and sees the first's commit -
  one admitted; lending's L6 → L7 and bnpl's L6 → (P), no transaction holding another module's row before L6, so no cycle.
- **Refinements to the wording (and why):** the operator capital read is `LendingCapitalDesk.capital()`, not
  `LendingCapitalAdministration` (which reads no headroom figure) - its `outstandingMinor` is the one wider figure, the
  `Headroom` record keeping its shape (no loan/BNPL split - an owner judgement, below); the port returns bnpl's own
  `BnplHeadroom(currency, headroom)`, not lending's `Headroom` (ADR-0104 decision 3's "the `Headroom` record" is
  unreachable from bnpl without the refused edge); "`LendingCapitalProof` sums …" - the proof keeps no copy of the
  formula and reads the one headroom, so its BNPL term is the headroom's and the backlog's second probe became "the
  proof's headroom arm judged without the outstanding term"; `BnplCapitalDatabaseTest` lives in `app`'s
  `com.finapp.app.lending` package (it reuses that package's origination fixtures, `LoanApplicationDatabaseTest.terms`)
  and is registered `own-container` (it plants capital as `LendingCreditExposureDatabaseTest` does); "a loan acceptance
  holding L6" is the real `LoanAcceptances.accept` on the suite's connection, uncommitted, and "a BNPL judgement holding
  L6" the port on the suite's connection with the BNPL principal it funds planted before the commit (what `-013`'s
  capital step will do); `LendingCapitalDatabaseTest#theLastCapitalRefusesAnAcceptanceBesideAPlantedBnplPrincipal`
  judges through that suite's own headroom consumer - the very `underLock(…).admits(…)` every lending consumer calls -
  the real acceptance beside BNPL being `BnplCapitalDatabaseTest`'s; the capital report's as-of-date fold
  (`LendingReports`, `P11-TSK-030`) is in scope - the gate's IMPORTANT; `PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §2.1's "BNPL committed and
  outstanding" corrected to outstanding only.
- **Gate** (2026-10-17): NOT COMPLETE on its first pass - IMPORTANT, `LendingReports.capital` (the audited as-of-date
  capital report, `GET /v1/operator/reports/lending/capital`) folded `LENDING_CAPITAL`, `LOAN_PRINCIPAL` and
  `LOAN_PRINCIPAL_DUE` by literal - a second copy of the formula that would have over-stated headroom and under-stated
  `lending_funded` as soon as a BNPL line exists; fixed by folding `LendingCapitalHeadroom.principalPurposes()`, and
  `LendingReportsDatabaseTest`'s capital section now plants BNPL principal before holding the report equal to
  `atRest` (written, not run). MINOR, recorded: the wording refinements above. Then COMPLETE. **"Would this remain
  correct if 10 instances executed it concurrently?" — `PASS`**: the judgement is a read under one database row lock in
  the caller's transaction (no JVM state, no cache, no instance clock); ten consumers of one currency's capital on ten
  instances - lending's or bnpl's - serialise on that row and each re-reads every term after the holder commits; the
  outstanding term is one statement, so a concurrent billing, repayment or refund is wholly in or out and can only read
  low; a failed read fails the caller. The counted proofs (`BnplCapitalDatabaseTest`, `LendingCapitalDatabaseTest`
  orders 15 to 20) are written and owed their first run - the verdict rests on the same row lock lending's counted races
  proved in Phase 11 and on the hermetic lock-and-order cases. **Probes** (`MUTATION_TESTING.md` §2, ten rows, each
  caught on its first run and restored byte-identical by sha256): `BNPL_PRINCIPAL_DUE` dropped; `BNPL_PRINCIPAL`
  dropped; the proof's headroom arm without the outstanding term; the port on `atRest`; the committed term read after
  the outstanding; the outstanding term as two statements; `BNPL_MERCHANT_FEE_INCOME` in the set (two guards); `admits`
  one unit past; the port answering zero on a failed read. **Not run** (owner's instruction): the database cases named
  in §Tests and `LendingReportsDatabaseTest`'s planted BNPL principal, and the backlog's three live probes. **Owner
  judgements:** a loan/BNPL split of the outstanding term in the operator reports (one figure today); the write-off
  finding for Phase 14 (ADR-0104 §Follow-up); the headroom's one statement now folds every BNPL principal line under
  L6 - its cost grows with history (the contention debt row widened).
- **Objective**: one capital pool, one proof — BNPL principal is counted in lending's capital headroom from the instant
  it exists, and bnpl can judge headroom under L6 in its own transaction (B2, ADR-0104, `INV-LND-13` extended,
  `INV-BNPL-10`).
- **Bounded context**: Lending (capital); BNPL (the port); `app` (the adapter).
- **Dependencies**: `-003`.
- **Scope**: lending's `LendingCapitalHeadroom` — `underLock` and `atRest` — and `LendingCapitalProof` sum
  `BNPL_PRINCIPAL + BNPL_PRINCIPAL_DUE` **by ledger purpose across every account of the currency**, beside
  `LOAN_PRINCIPAL + LOAN_PRINCIPAL_DUE`, in the same one statement (`PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §12.9) — ledger purposes, not bnpl
  types, so lending learns nothing of the bnpl module; BNPL has no committed-but-undisbursed principal, so the committed
  term gains no BNPL arm; `Headroom.lendingFunded()` adds the BNPL principal (the safeguarding adjustment, ADR-0096 §Why
  — BNPL creates merchant-payable liabilities without cash entering); bnpl's port `BnplCapital.underLock(uow,
  currency)` returning bnpl's own `BnplHeadroom` record, implemented in `app` (`LendingBnplCapital`) over
  `LendingCapitalHeadroom.underLock` — L6 is the currency's `LENDING_CAPITAL` row `FOR UPDATE`, taken in bnpl's
  transaction; `LendingBooksHaveOnePosterTest` and `BnplBooksHaveOnePosterTest` unchanged in meaning (lending reads the
  BNPL purposes, never posts them); lending's acceptance, draw and reversal races re-run unchanged; the
  `DISTRIBUTED_EXECUTION.md` §3 L6 row names bnpl as a holder.
- **Out of scope**: the acceptance that consumes headroom (`-013`); a BNPL reversal re-instating principal (`-024`); a
  separate BNPL pool or tranche (§20); capital return (owner item #4, open).
- **Domain changes**: the headroom's principal set; the `BnplCapital` port.
- **Persistence**: none (Java only; lending's next free stays `V031`).
- **APIs**: none; the operator capital read (`LendingCapitalAdministration`) shows the wider outstanding.
- **Events**: none.
- **Policy/model versioning**: none; the proof's formula is versioned by this change and recorded in ADR-0104.
- **Financial impact**: headroom now falls by every unit of BNPL principal outstanding and rises by every repayment or
  refund at commit; merchant fee income is not capital (lending A29).
- **Invariants**: `INV-LND-13` (extended), `INV-BNPL-10`, `INV-BAL-05`.
- **Distributed-system concerns**: a BNPL judgement under `BnplCapital.underLock` and a loan acceptance racing for the
  last capital in a currency → serialised on L6, one admitted (lock-wait asserting the waiting statement, both orders);
  a BNPL principal line committing during `atRest` → never torn (one statement). `PASS` on the counts of
  `LendingCapitalDatabaseTest` and `BnplCapitalDatabaseTest` — the BNPL principal written by owner-role journal fixtures
  on `BNPL_OBLIGATION` accounts (the `P11-TSK-013` precedent), re-asserted through the real purchase by `-013`.
- **Idempotency**: N/A — a read under a lock inside the caller's transaction.
- **Consistency**: headroom derived from journal lines under L6, never from `account_balance`.
- **Atomicity**: the caller's transaction.
- **Failure handling**: a failed read fails the caller's transaction — never a headroom of zero or of the old formula.
- **Security**: no new door; no figure in a log, tag or span.
- **Audit**: none new.
- **Observability**: the existing capital gauges (`finapp.lending.capital.headroom.low`) now count BNPL principal —
  their tests extended.
- **Reconciliation implications**: `LendingCapitalProof` gains the BNPL term (capital recognised from bank evidence =
  headroom + committed + loan and BNPL principal outstanding); the safeguarding position's lending-funded adjustment
  widened.
- **Tests**: lending's `LendingCapitalDatabaseTest` (`#aBnplPrincipalLineLowersTheHeadroom`,
  `#bnplPrincipalDueStillCounts`, `#aRepaidBnplPrincipalRestoresTheHeadroom`, `#theCapitalProofCountsBnplPrincipal`,
  `#lendingFundedIncludesBnplPrincipal`, `#theLastCapitalRefusesAnAcceptanceBesideAPlantedBnplPrincipal`); `app`'s
  `BnplCapitalDatabaseTest` (`#aBnplJudgementAndALoanAcceptanceSerialiseOnTheCapitalRow` (lock-wait, both orders),
  `#theLastCapitalAdmitsOne`); re-run unchanged: `LoanAcceptanceDatabaseTest#acceptancesRacingForTheLastCapitalAdmitOne`,
  `CreditLineDrawDatabaseTest#drawingTakesTheLineThenTheCapital`; `LendingCapitalAdministrationTest` and the capital
  gauges' tests extended.
- **Probe**: drop `BNPL_PRINCIPAL_DUE` from the principal set → `#bnplPrincipalDueStillCounts` red; leave the proof's
  BNPL term out → `#theCapitalProofCountsBnplPrincipal` red; read headroom without the L6 lock in the port →
  `#aBnplJudgementAndALoanAcceptanceSerialiseOnTheCapitalRow` red.
- **Acceptance criteria**: capital headroom and the capital proof count loan and BNPL principal alike, from journal
  lines, under one lock; lending's Phase 11 races stay green.
- **Definition of done**: `DOD-FIN` (capital; F2, F6, F7 binding; F1, F3, F4, F5 vacuous — a read; F8: the capital
  proof's BNPL term). **Risk**: High. **Cx**: S.

**P12-TSK-006 — Merchant BNPL enablement and fee schedule** — `COMPLETE` (2026-10-17; started by the owner beside `P12-TSK-007` — Phase 12 wave A; marked `READY` by `P12-TSK-005`'s completion gate; its dependency `-002` `COMPLETE`; marks `P12-TSK-010` `READY` at its merge-in, the coordinator's instruction - `-010`'s last dependency)
- **Objective**: a merchant can offer BNPL only after a four-eyes enablement, priced by its own BNPL fee schedule, with
  the fee version pinned per purchase and one fee arithmetic for the split and the return (OQ-8, B8; ADR-0058, ADR-0102).
- **Bounded context**: Merchant; BNPL (the port); `app` (the operator doors, the adapter).
- **Dependencies**: `-002`.
- **Scope**: **merchant `V010`**: `merchant_bnpl_enablement` (per merchant: `PROPOSED → ACTIVE | REJECTED`, `ACTIVE →
  WITHDRAWN`; proposer, approver and reasons; `CHECK (approved_by <> proposed_by)` — the payout-destination four-eyes
  precedent; one live proposal per merchant by partial unique; withdrawal a single-operator, risk-reducing act — the
  suspension precedent, the design's to confirm), `merchant_bnpl_fee_schedule` (the assignment per (merchant, product)
  of an existing `fee_schedule` whose versions carry `refund_fee_policy = RETURNED` — B3's pro-rated return; a
  `RETAINED` schedule refused), and `bnpl_fee_pin` (`UNIQUE (purchase_id)`; merchant, product, `fee_schedule_version_id`;
  `INSERT`-only — the intent-keyed `payment_fee_pin` cannot hold a purchase); the doors
  `POST /v1/operator/merchants/{id}/bnpl-enablement` (+ `/{proposalId}/approval`, `/rejection`, `/withdrawal`;
  `MERCHANT_ADMINISTER`, `Idempotency-Key` `merchant.bnpl-enablement:EMPLOYEE:<id>`) and
  `PUT /v1/operator/merchants/{merchantId}/bnpl-fee-schedules/{product}` (`FEE_ADMINISTER`, reasoned, converging — the
  existing `…/fee-schedule` precedent); bnpl's port `BnplMerchants`, implemented in `app` over merchant:
  `standing(uow, merchantRef, product)` (`merchant.merchant` `FOR SHARE` as `CheckoutSessions.requireTrading` does —
  `ACTIVE`, an `ACTIVE` enablement, an assigned BNPL schedule with an effective version), `payableAccount(uow,
  merchantRef, currency)`, `pinFee(uow, merchantRef, product, purchaseId, gross)` (the pin born and the split returned:
  `f = round_HALF_EVEN(G · bps / 10 000) + fixed` through `FeeCalculation.assess`, `gross = fee + net` exactly, `f < G`
  else a typed `BelowFee` — `SaleBelowFeeException`'s rule), and `returnedFee(uow, purchaseId, refundedBefore,
  refunded)` through `FeeCalculation.returnedFee` under the pinned version (the cumulative difference that telescopes to
  exactly `f`, `PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §12.5 — BNPL refunds are synchronous, so the exact share, never
  `leastReturnedFee`'s conservative one).
- **Out of scope**: the purchase that pins (`-013`); the payable's drill-down (`-016`); the merchant-key refund door and
  its scope (`-021`); merchant credit limits (§20); customer-facing fees (none on P4, OQ-17).
- **Domain changes**: `BnplEnablement`, the BNPL schedule assignment, `BnplFeePin`; `BnplMerchants`.
- **Persistence**: merchant `V010`.
- **APIs**: the two operator doors; errors `merchant.BnplEnablementPending`, `merchant.SelfApprovalRefused` (the
  merchant module's spelling, the design to align with the existing payout-destination code),
  `merchant.BnplScheduleNotReturning` — catalogued in `ERROR_CONTRACT.md` by this task.
- **Events**: none — no consumer (Phase 10's reasoning: an event nobody consumes is refused); the facts are audited.
- **Policy/model versioning**: the BNPL fee schedule's versions are existing immutable `fee_schedule_version` rows
  (`INV-MER-03`); the pin fixes the version per purchase.
- **Financial impact**: decides the merchant discount and its return for every BNPL purchase; moves no money itself.
- **Invariants**: `INV-MER-03`, `INV-MER-04` (the returned fee across refunds), `INV-BNPL-04` (the split conserves the
  gross), `INV-MER-01`.
- **Distributed-system concerns**: ten concurrent proposals for one merchant → one live, nine `409
  merchant.BnplEnablementPending`; an approval and a rejection racing → exactly one; ten pins for one purchase → one
  (`UNIQUE (purchase_id)`, the second refused, never a second version); a suspension racing a standing read →
  serialised on the merchant row's `FOR SHARE`. `PASS` on the counts of `MerchantBnplEnablementDatabaseTest`.
- **Idempotency**: the claim per employee; the conditional edges; the assignment converges; the pin's unique.
- **Consistency**: the standing read under `FOR SHARE` in the caller's transaction; the pin and the split from one
  version read once.
- **Atomicity**: the pin in the caller's (the purchase's) transaction — a rollback leaves no pin.
- **Failure handling**: a `RETAINED` schedule, a missing version or a sale below its fee → typed refusals before any
  write; a self-approval refused and audited `FAILED` (R4).
- **Security**: `MERCHANT_ADMINISTER` four-eyes for enablement; `FEE_ADMINISTER` for the assignment; reasons
  `RESTRICTED-PII`; no merchant-key door here.
- **Audit**: `merchant.BnplEnablementProposed`, `…Approved`, `…Rejected`, `…Withdrawn`, the refused self-approval,
  `merchant.BnplFeeScheduleAssigned` — catalogued in `AUDITABLE_ACTIONS.md` by this task.
- **Observability**: none new (the purchase meter is `-013`'s).
- **Reconciliation implications**: the three-way proof's fee arm (`-025`) recomputes each purchase's fee and return
  under its pin.
- **Tests**: `MerchantBnplEnablementDatabaseTest` (`app`: `#enablementIsFourEyes`, `#theProposerCannotApprove` (audited
  `FAILED`), `#oneLiveProposalPerMerchant` (ten proposers), `#approvalAndRejectionLeaveExactlyOne`,
  `#aRetainedScheduleIsRefusedForBnpl`, `#theFeePinIsBornOncePerPurchase` (ten pinners),
  `#thePinIsNeverUpdatedOrDeletedByAnyRole`, `#aSuspendedMerchantIsNotEnabled`, `#aWithdrawnEnablementOffersNothing`);
  `BnplMerchantFeeSplitPropertiesTest` (`gross = fee + net` exactly for every gross and version, `f < G` or refused, the
  returned fee over every refund sequence summing to `G` telescoping to exactly `f`, never exceeding `f` in any
  interleaving); `BnplMerchantEndpointDatabaseTest` (permissions, keyed replay, negatives); `MerchantMigrationTest`
  extended.
- **Probe**: drop the domain check and the `approved_by <> proposed_by` `CHECK` → `#theProposerCannotApprove` red; drop
  `UNIQUE (purchase_id)` → `#theFeePinIsBornOncePerPurchase` red; return the fee by each refund's own rounded share →
  the telescoping property red.
- **Acceptance criteria**: a merchant is BNPL-enabled only by two people; its BNPL fee is computed once per purchase
  under a pinned version, conserves the gross, and returns exactly `f` across any full refund.
- **Definition of done**: `DOD-FIN` (the merchant fee; F3, F6, F7 binding; F1, F2, F4, F5 vacuous — no posting here,
  the fee posts in `-013`; F8: the three-way proof's fee arm, `-025`), `DOD-SEC`, `DOD-API`. **Risk**: Medium.
  **Cx**: M.
- **Design** (2026-10-17, the three-command loop run straight through on the owner's instruction): the enablement is
  merchant's machine and the pin merchant's fact; bnpl sees both only through its own port. **Merchant**
  (`V010`): `merchant_bnpl_enablement` - `PROPOSED -> ACTIVE | REJECTED`, `ACTIVE -> WITHDRAWN` (`BnplEnablementStatus`),
  each decision whole and frozen on the row (the row is its own history: no `_event` table beside the audit trail),
  one live (proposed or active) per merchant by partial unique, four eyes as
  `merchant_bnpl_enablement_approver_is_not_proposer` (`decided_by <> proposed_by` for every approved state), every
  instant `clock_timestamp()` in the edge trigger after the lock, clamped forward (the Phase 11 gate's stamp lesson);
  `merchant_bnpl_fee_schedule` + `_event` (V004's pointer per (merchant, product), a trigger refusing a schedule with
  any `RETAINED` version for every writer); `bnpl_fee_pin` (the purchase the primary key, merchant, product, version,
  the gross - no fee or net stored -, `pinned_at` on the application clock, the fee schedules' own basis; insert-only,
  V004's immutability function reused, no truncate; a trigger holding it to a returning version of the assigned
  schedule in force by `pinned_at`, in the gross's currency, for an enabled merchant). Services `BnplEnablements`
  (propose / approve / reject / withdraw; lock-then-look; the same person's retry converges; a self-approval thrown so
  the act rolls back whole, `recordRefusal` writing it `FAILED` in a transaction of its own - R4) and `BnplPricing`
  (assign; `standing` - merchant `FOR SHARE`, then its `ACTIVE` enablement `FOR SHARE`, then the assignment and the
  version in force; `pin` - the standing re-judged, the version read once after the locks, `FeeCalculation.assess`,
  the sale refused unless the net is positive, the pin inserted; `returnedFee` - `FeeCalculation.returnedFee` under
  the pinned version). **bnpl**: the port `BnplMerchants` (`standing`, `payableAccount`, `pinFee` returning bnpl's
  `MerchantFeeSplit` - `G = f + net` re-asserted, `0 <= f < G` -, `returnedFee`; refusals `NotOffered(standing)`,
  `BelowFee`, `AlreadyPinned`, `NotPinned`); the merchant by value as a `UUID` (agreed with `-007` on the board).
  **app**: `MerchantBnplMerchants` (the adapter), `MerchantBnplDesk` / `MerchantBnplController` (five routes),
  `MerchantBnplBeans`. Multi-instance: ten proposers - one live (the index, a savepoint); a decision race - one (the
  row lock and the conditional write); ten pinners - one (the key); a suspension, re-assignment or withdrawal against
  a standing read - serialised on the share locks; no JVM state. Financial chain: no posting here (the fee posts in
  F1, `-013`); the split conserves by subtraction; the return telescopes to exactly f.
- **As built** (2026-10-17): merchant `V010` (`V010__bnpl_enablement_and_fee_schedule.sql`), merchant's

  `MerchantClosedException`'s message generalised; bnpl's `BnplMerchants`, `MerchantFeeSplit`; `app`'s
  `MerchantBnplMerchants`, `MerchantBnplDesk`, `MerchantBnplController`, `MerchantBnplBeans`. Suites: merchant's

  20,000 splits over every rounding policy and 0/2/3-minor-unit currencies, 3,000 refund sequences in three orders

  `MerchantOnboardingDatabaseTest`'s sweep extended over the pin. **Refinements of this entry's wording**: (1) the

  its own transaction (R4) while the payout destination keeps its older `DENIED`-in-one-transaction shape, untouched;
  (4) the withdrawal is confirmed a single-operator act (the suspension precedent), on `ACTIVE` only; a proposer's
  change of mind is a rejection, which anyone may make; a closed merchant takes no proposal and no approval

  actor's type (`BnplTermsDesk`'s A5-04 note); (6) `standing` returns the first failing condition
  (`ENABLED | NOT_TRADING | NOT_ENABLED | NOT_PRICED`) rather than a boolean, so `-010` can map it, and an unknown or
  non-merchant reference is `NOT_TRADING`, one answer; (7) a `RETAINED` version added to a BNPL schedule after its
  assignment (no lock can arbitrate it - V004) is caught where it would price: the product is `NOT_PRICED` and the pin
  refused, never a `RETAINED` BNPL fee; (8) the fee's rounding is the pinned version's policy (`INV-MON-03`); A8's and
  `INV-BNPL-04`'s `HALF_EVEN` is the default an operator gives a BNPL version, not a refusal of the others - an owner
  judgement; (9) `PHASE_12_PLAN.md` section 3.3 and `MODULE_ARCHITECTURE.md` said the returned fee came "through its
  least-share arithmetic" - corrected to the exact cumulative share section 12.5 and ADR-0105 decide; (10) no read
  door: the backlog names none, reasons are never served, and the four act receipts carry the state.

- **As built** (2026-10-17): checkout `V004` - `checkout_session.financed_by_ref uuid` (the purchase by value), `CHECK (financed_by_ref IS NULL OR (status = 'COMPLETED' AND payment_intent_ref IS NULL))` (never both, never late, never pending), the partial unique `checkout_session_one_session_per_financing`, the edge trigger replaced whole (`OPEN → {PAYMENT_PENDING, COMPLETED, EXPIRED, ABANDONED}`; the financing reference set once and only on `OPEN → COMPLETED`; that edge only with it, no intent, and `OLD.expires_at > statement_timestamp()`), the deferred `checkout_session_financed_beside_its_order` (an edge commits only beside its order), `GRANT UPDATE (financed_by_ref)`; `CheckoutSessionStatus` (`OPEN` reaches `COMPLETED`, `isFinancingEdge`), `CheckoutSession.completeByFinancing(databaseNow, purchase)` / `financingRefusalAt` / `financedByRef` / `completedAs` (`CheckoutCompletion`: `COMPLETED`, `COMPLETED_LATE`, `FINANCED`; `FinancingRefusal`: `NOT_OPEN`, `EXPIRED`), `complete()` held to `PAYMENT_PENDING`; the store's `databaseNow` (its own statement, after the lock) and conditional `completeByFinancing` (re-judging the deadline at the trigger's instant); `CheckoutSessionToken.presented(Sensitive)`; `app`'s `CheckoutSessions.lockForFinancing` (B3) and `completedByFinancing` (the order with the financing entry, `ORDER_CREATED` audited with `financedBy`, `checkout.OrderPaid` `completedAs = FINANCED`, the `financed` meters), bnpl's port `BnplCheckoutSessions` (`read` by token → `Session(sessionRef, merchantRef, gross, expiresAt, open, expired)`; `lockForPurchase` → `Payable` | `NotPayable(NOT_OPEN | EXPIRED)`; `completeByFinancing` → `Completed(orderRef)` | `NotPayable`), `app`'s `CheckoutBnplSessions` wired in `BnplBeans`; the session read's additive `completedAs`; the confirmation refusing a financed session `409 checkout.NotConfirmable` (it was a latent `500`: the paid branch demanded an intent).
- **Refinements to the wording (and why):** `completedAs` already existed on `checkout.OrderPaid` (Phase 6: `COMPLETED` / `COMPLETED_LATE`), so `FINANCED` is a third *value* of the published field, event version 1 unchanged, and the session read gains the same field - one vocabulary (`CheckoutCompletion`), derived, never stored; the confirm door's refusal of `"BNPL"` is its existing `422 platform.ValidationFailed` (the entry's "400"), asserted unchanged, and the plan §3.3's "routed to the BNPL application" is confirmed read as "the application is its own door"; the expiry judgement is made three times - B3 after the lock, the aggregate on the same database instant, and the conditional write's own predicate at the trigger's instant - so a purchase whose work crosses the deadline is refused typed and rolls back, never a trigger error; "beside its evidence" at the database rank is the order (deferred) plus the set-once, one-per-purchase financing reference - the purchase's own half is bnpl's (`-013`), since no schema reads another's (ADR-0029); the financing entry in `CheckoutFinancingDatabaseTest` is a by-value identifier (the column has no foreign key), re-asserted against F1 by `-013`; `CheckoutConfirmEndpointTest` is hermetic over the door's two extracted decisions (`instrumentChoice`, `refuseAFinancedSession`) - `TestTaxonomyTest` reads any `DataSource` as a database need, and the over-HTTP halves are the database suite's; the suite is own-container because its expiry race runs the unscoped sweeper on skewed clocks.
- **Gate** (2026-10-17): NOT COMPLETE on its first pass - **IMPORTANT**, the port's unlocked `read` gave bnpl the session's `expiresAt` and checkout's `OPEN` but no judgement of the deadline on the database clock, so the application door (`-010`) and the offer sweep (`-011`) would have had to judge "unexpired" on an instance clock (PHASE_12_PLAN.md §7: every window judged on `statement_timestamp()`); repaired - `Session.expired`, judged on the database clock read after the row (`CheckoutSessions.databaseNow`), held by `CheckoutBnplSessionsTest#theReadJudgesTheDeadlineOnTheDatabaseClock` and its probe. MINOR, recorded: the `financed` meters count inside the purchase's transaction, so a T-pur rolled back after the completion overcounts by one - the capture's own recorded compromise (`CheckoutMeters`); `completedByFinancing` takes the session lock itself (re-entrant), so a caller skipping B3 would take the session after (P) - the port's contract (lock, judge, then complete) is `-013`'s to honour and its counted race to prove. Then COMPLETE. **Multi-instance: PASS** - the row lock and the conditional write (ten completions, one order, `UNIQUE (session_ref)` behind it); a confirmation's conditional `OPEN → PAYMENT_PENDING` the other arbiter (the loser refused `NotPayable` or `409 checkout.NotConfirmable`); the expiry sweeper's lock-then-judge (exactly one of `COMPLETED`, `EXPIRED`, whatever the skew); every judgement on the database clock after the lock; `V004` binding every writer. **Twelve probes caught**, restores sha256-verified, MUTATION_TESTING §2 +11 rows (the twelfth - the order announced `COMPLETED` rather than `FINANCED` - is an event-shape probe, recorded here, no invariant row). `CheckoutFinancingDatabaseTest` (own-container, ten cases) written, not run (owner's instruction); the backlog's two live probes owed. - **Objective**: a checkout session can be completed by financing — exactly once, never beside a card or wallet payment
  of the same session, never after its expiry — so the merchant sees one order whatever paid for it (ADR-0053,
  `INV-MER-06`, `PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §5.2a).

- **Dependencies**: `-002`.

  `EXPIRED → COMPLETED_LATE` stays intent-only); checkout's `CheckoutSession.completeByFinancing` (from `OPEN` only,

  BNPL purchase (§2.1 refuses a "BNPL rail").
- **Domain changes**: the new edge; `financed_by_ref`; `completeByFinancing`; `BnplCheckoutSessions`.

- **APIs**: none new; the session read and the merchant's order read show `completedAs = FINANCED`; the confirm door's
  `400` for `"BNPL"` asserted.
- **Events**: `checkout.OrderPaid` with `completedAs` (additive).
- **Policy/model versioning**: none.
- **Financial impact**: none in checkout (checkout holds no money); the order references the financing entry.
- **Invariants**: `INV-MER-06` (one order per session), `INV-LIFE-02`, `INV-LIFE-04`, `INV-BNPL-03` (one session, at
  most one purchase — checkout's half).
- **Distributed-system concerns**: a completion by financing racing a card or wallet confirmation of one session on two
  instances → exactly one wins (the confirmation moved it `OPEN → PAYMENT_PENDING` first, or the financing completed
  it), the loser refused (`NotPayable`; checkout's existing `409 checkout.NotConfirmable`), both orders asserted; a
  completion racing the expiry sweeper at `expires_at` ± 1 µs under ±5 s instance skew → exactly one of `COMPLETED`,
  `EXPIRED`; ten completions of one session → one order. `PASS` on the counts of `CheckoutFinancingDatabaseTest`, the
  financing entry a journal fixture until `-013`.
- **Idempotency**: the edge's conditional from-set; `financed_by_ref` set once; the order's `UNIQUE (session_ref)`.
- **Consistency**: the session judged under its row lock on the database clock; the lock order's (c) argument
  (`PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §7.3) holds — a capture completes only a `PAYMENT_PENDING` session, which a financing never
  completes.
- **Atomicity**: the edge, the order and the event in the caller's transaction; a rollback leaves the session `OPEN`.
- **Failure handling**: a session not `OPEN` or expired → `NotPayable` with nothing written; a direct write of the edge
  without `financed_by_ref` refused by the trigger for every role.
- **Security**: the session read by its token (never logged or echoed — `ConfirmSessionRequest`'s rule); no new door.
- **Audit**: none new (the purchase's audit is `-013`'s).
- **Observability**: the existing checkout meters gain the `FINANCED` completion tag, registered eagerly.
- **Reconciliation implications**: the merchant's order references the financing entry, which the three-way proof's
  merchant arm (`-025`) reads.
