**P12-TSK-015 — Instalment billing, the catch-up application and the servicing schedule** — `COMPLETE` (2026-10-18; started beside `-014` and `-016`, Phase 12 wave B, branch `P12-TSK-015`, bnpl `V008`; its dependency `-013` `COMPLETE`; marks `P12-TSK-017` `READY` - `-018` depends on `-015` alone too)
- **Objective**: on each due date exactly what is due becomes due — P4's instalments 2–4 on `D1 + 14(k−1)`,
  PN's on its monthly dates with the interest actually accrued, never the projection — and money already
  held pays what is due, at a billing's birth and whenever something is already past due (the Phase 11
  gate's R2, applied from bnpl's first servicing table); the servicing sweep every later step rides on.
- **Bounded context**: BNPL; Ledger.
- **Dependencies**: `-013`.
- **Scope**: `bnpl V008`: `bnpl_billing` (`UNIQUE (instalment_id)`; principal due, PN interest due, agreement
  and schedule versions, business date, entry by value; INSERT-only) — **extending** the table `-013` created for P4's
  instalment 1 (T-pur's F2; reconciled by the transition's consistency pass, 2026-10-16);
  `bnpl_credit_balance_application` with its allocation rows, two occasions on one table (lending `V029`'s
  shape): **at a billing's birth** (`UNIQUE (billing_id)`, key `bnpl.credit-application:<billing>`) and
  **catch-up** (billing null, `catch_up_sequence` ≥ 1, `UNIQUE (obligation_id, catch_up_sequence)`, key
  `bnpl.credit-application:<obligation>:catch-up:<n>`), held at commit by a deferred conservation (the rows
  sum to the application; no billed component paid beyond what it billed); `bnpl.billing_component_paid
  (billing, component)` — the one definition later tasks replace; **the principal value floor**
  `bnpl.principal_value_floor(obligation)` (created by `-013`, extended here) — the later of the day after the obligation's latest accrual
  (PN) and its latest billing date, never before the purchase's business date — read under B4 by every
  writer of a fact that moves principal or the accrual base (applications here; repayments, collections,
  refund cancellations, reversals and payoffs in later tasks), which values it `max(today, floor)`, a trigger
  refusing any raw writer below it (R1 applied from the first table); a billing is a base-neutral
  reclassification dated its due date, never before the latest billing's. `BnplServicingSchedule`
  (leaderless, `SmartLifecycle`, off in test contexts; one `SKIP LOCKED` statement claims `ACTIVE`
  obligations with `next_servicing_at <= statement_timestamp()`, the permit re-stamped by the database to
  the next business date's start in the pinned zone (A22) or a retry cadence for a failing obligation);
  T-svc's skeleton (`PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §7.1): **(B4)** the obligation `FOR UPDATE`, the database clock read
  after it; **the accrual gate** — for PN every elapsed date through the business date's eve accrued, else
  nothing is written, the step answers `BEHIND_ACCRUAL` and T-acc (`-017`) runs first in its own
  transaction (until `-017` lands, PN billing is exercised behind an owner-role accrual fixture — the Phase 11
  precedent; `-017` re-asserts it through real accruals); billing of every instalment whose due date has
  arrived, oldest first (F2: `DR BNPL_PRINCIPAL_DUE p / CR BNPL_PRINCIPAL p`; PN also `DR BNPL_INTEREST_DUE
  i / CR BNPL_INTEREST_ACCRUED i`, `i` = Σ the period's posted accruals; key `bnpl.billing:<instalment>`);
  then the at-billing application and the catch-up application over past-due items whenever credit is held
  and something is due (F3a, `ALLOCATION_ENGINE_V1` through `creditmath`: oldest due first, `FEES → INTEREST
  → PRINCIPAL`), each value-dated at the floor rule — **after billing and before** the steps `-019`
  (collection), `-018` (closure) and `-020` (condition, late fee) add, in that fixed order under B4;
  `InstalmentDue`; the customer's schedule read extended with billed and paid status; P4's instalment 1,
  billed in T-pur, never billed again (the unique); `LEASE_PROTECTED_SCHEDULERS` +1 with its
  `DISTRIBUTED_EXECUTION.md` §3 row.
- **Out of scope**: PN accrual (`-017`); repayment and closure (`-018`); auto-collection (`-019`); conditions
  and late fees (`-020`); the dispute hold (`-023`).
- **Domain changes**: `BnplBilling`, `BnplCreditBalanceApplication`, `BnplServicing` (the step and its fixed
  order), `BnplReceivables` (the due-state derivation from billings and allocations — one derivation for
  every later caller), `ServicingOutcome`.
- **Persistence**: `bnpl V008`.
- **APIs**: `GET /v1/me/bnpl-agreements/{id}/schedule` extended (billed, paid, due) — owner-scoped; no new
  route, no new error.
- **Events**: `InstalmentDue` (instalment, due date, principal and PN interest due).
- **Policy/model versioning**: each billing names the agreement, schedule and engine versions; each
  application its allocation engine version — all from the pinned agreement version.
- **Financial impact**: F2 — the same claim reclassified as due (DPD readable from the ledger); F3a — money
  already held settles what is due, so no arrears stand beside held credit.
- **Invariants**: `INV-BNPL-01`, `INV-BNPL-05` (the last instalment bills the remaining principal),
  `INV-LND-02` by analogy (PN bills accrued interest), `INV-LND-04` by analogy (allocation), `INV-IDEM-02`,
  `INV-BAL-04`, `INV-HIST-01`.
- **Distributed-system concerns**: billing run twice or by ten sweepers → one billing per instalment (the
  unique, the ledger key, B4); billing racing a customer repayment (`-018`) on the due date → serialised on
  B4; credit held while an item is past due → applied by the next step's catch-up, never left beside arrears;
  midnight under ±5 s instance skew → the database clock decides the business date; the scheduler down three
  days → each missed instalment billed at its own due date, every application floored; a failing obligation
  re-stamps its permit and never holds the page. `PASS` on the counts of `BnplBillingDatabaseTest`.
- **Idempotency**: born once per instalment plus `bnpl.billing:<instalment>`; the at-billing application
  once per billing; a catch-up application once per number per obligation.
- **Consistency**: the due state derived under B4 from rows, never the projection; PN billing only after the
  period's accruals exist, judged under B4.
- **Atomicity**: the billing, its entry, the applications, their entries, the event and its outbox row in
  one transaction step.
- **Failure handling**: a missing accrual writes nothing (`BEHIND_ACCRUAL`); a crash re-drives from rows; a
  failing obligation backs off by the retry cadence.
- **Security**: a system act with no door; the schedule read owner-scoped (another party's id → `404`).
- **Audit**: none — a scheduled process's rows and entries are its trail.
- **Observability**: `finapp.bnpl.billing{product, outcome}` and `finapp.bnpl.servicing{step, outcome}`
  (added to `PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §15's list by this task — the plan names no servicing series),
  `finapp.bnpl.servicing.sweeper.enabled`; a span per step (`BnplFlowScope`, no attributes).
- **Reconciliation implications**: `BNPL_PRINCIPAL_DUE` and `BNPL_INTEREST_DUE` explained by billings less
  allocations and applications — the subledger proof's arms (`-025`).
- **Tests**: `BnplBillingDatabaseTest` (`#billedOnTheDueDateOnce`, `#tenSweepersBillOnce`,
  `#p4BillsEveryFourteenDays`, `#instalmentOneIsNeverBilledTwice`, `#pnBillsTheAccruedInterestNotTheProjection`
  (the owner-role accrual fixture; re-asserted by `-017`), `#billingWaitsForEveryAccrualOfThePeriod`,
  `#theLastInstalmentBillsTheRemainder`, `#aCreditBalancePaysTheBill` (an owner-role credit fixture;
  re-asserted by `-018`), `#heldCreditSettlesWhatIsAlreadyPastDue` (R2), `#threeMissedDueDatesBillAtTheirDueDates`,
  `#noApplicationBelowTheFloor` (R1: a clock stepped back across midnight; the trigger refusing a raw
  writer), `#skewNeverBillsEarly`, `#aFailingObligationDoesNotHoldThePage`, `#servicingTakesTheObligationLock`
  (lock-wait on B4)); `NoSingleInstanceAssumptionRulesTest` (+1).
- **Probe**: drop `UNIQUE (instalment_id)` → `#tenSweepersBillOnce` red; bill the projection's interest →
  `#pnBillsTheAccruedInterestNotTheProjection` red; skip the catch-up application →
  `#heldCreditSettlesWhatIsAlreadyPastDue` red; value an application `today` instead of at the floor →
  `#noApplicationBelowTheFloor` red.
- **Acceptance criteria**: Σ billed principal over an obligation's life = its principal less what refunds
  cancelled unbilled; billed interest = accrued interest; held credit never stands beside a past-due item
  at the end of a step.
- **Definition of done**: `DOD-FIN` (F1, F2, F3, F6, F7 binding; F4 vacuous — no billing is reversed, a
  refund cancels billed principal by its own entry (`-021`); F5 vacuous — no external event; F8: the
  subledger proof's due arms, `-025`). **Risk**: High. **Cx**: M.
- **As built** (2026-10-18): **bnpl `V008`** (`V008__instalment_billing_the_catch_up_application_and_the_servicing_permit.sql`)
  - `bnpl_billing` extended (schedule id, version and engine, agreement id and version, accrual engine, period start, the
  business date the trigger stamps, correlation - NULL only on a row before V008; `UNIQUE (obligation_id, value_date)`;
  a billing of nothing admitted, its entry NULL - lending V012's shape) and its trigger replaced: B4 re-taken for every
  writer, the latest schedule version and the agreement version in force, **dated its due date** once that date has come
  on the database clock (`business_date_latest`), oldest first, the period it closes, pay-in-N's interest exactly Σ the
  period's posted accruals with every date of the period accrued, the principal `least(remaining, max(0, amount -
  interest))` and the last instalment the remainder; the accrual RECORD `bnpl_interest_accrual` (`UNIQUE (obligation_id,
  accrual_date)`, append-only, SELECT only to the application role - its writer is `-017`'s); `bnpl.principal_value_floor`
  replaced with its accrual arm; `bnpl_credit_balance_application` + `_allocation` (two occasions, `UNIQUE (billing_id)`,
  `UNIQUE (obligation_id, catch_up_sequence)`, the next number and the floor's two ranks judged under B4 by the trigger,
  the deferred conservation); `bnpl.billing_component_paid` (credit applications + repayments' due-item lines) and
  `bnpl.billing_component_billed`; the obligation's edge function replaced to admit the permit's move alone, `GRANT UPDATE
  (next_servicing_at)`. bnpl's `BnplServicing` (T-svc), `BnplCreditBalanceApplications` (F3a, at billing and catch-up),
  `BnplReceivables` (the one due-state derivation, refused unless the rows explain the due accounts), `BnplBilling`,
  `BnplCreditBalanceApplication`, `ServicingOutcome`, `BnplServicingStore` / `JdbcBnplServicingStore`;
  `BnplPurchaseStore.insertBilling(BnplBilling)` (T-pur's instalment 1 now names its versions too) and `billedItems` (in
  place of `billedInstalments`); `app`'s `BnplServicingBeans`, `BnplServicingSchedule`, `BnplServicingMetrics`
  (`finapp.bnpl.billing{product, outcome}`, `finapp.bnpl.servicing{step, outcome}`, `finapp.bnpl.servicing.sweeper.enabled`;
  platform `MetricNames` gains `step`), the schedule view's `billedPrincipal`, `billedInterest`, `paid`, `due` (OpenAPI
  additions only). **The posting chain**: an instalment's due date comes → T-svc under B4 → F2 `DR BNPL_PRINCIPAL_DUE p /
  CR BNPL_PRINCIPAL p` (pay-in-N also `DR BNPL_INTEREST_DUE i / CR BNPL_INTEREST_ACCRUED i`, `i` = Σ the period's
  accruals), key `bnpl.billing:<instalment>`, posting date the business date, value date the due date → the same claim
  reclassified (`BNPL_PRINCIPAL + BNPL_PRINCIPAL_DUE` unchanged, the base of accrual untouched); then F3a `DR
  BNPL_CREDIT_BALANCE / CR <due accounts>` by `ALLOCATION_ENGINE_V1` oldest first `FEES -> INTEREST -> PRINCIPAL`, at the
  billing (`bnpl.credit-application:<billing>`) and as the catch-up (`…:<obligation>:catch-up:<n>`), value date `max(today,
  floor)` → credit held falls by exactly what the due accounts fall. **Refinements of the scope above, with reasons**: (1)
  the accrual RECORD is born here, SELECT-only - so billed interest is held to rows for every writer from the first
  billing and the floor's accrual arm exists from the first table; `-017` adds the writer (its entry records it); (2) a
  billing is dated its due date and posted on the business date (the plan's §12.11 "dated the business date" is the
  posting date; the scope's "dated its due date" the value date) - base-neutral, so the floor never forbids it; (3) the
  principal rule is lending's `least(remaining, max(0, amount - interest))`, which for pay-in-4 is exactly its scheduled
  principal - one rule for both products, held by the trigger to the rows; (4) the at-billing application spans every
  billed item still due (lending's), so a catch-up is born only when no billing of the step met the credit; (5) BEHIND_ACCRUAL
  leaves the claim's retry cadence as the permit (nothing written) - until `-017` lands every pay-in-N obligation past its
  purchase day is BEHIND_ACCRUAL each cadence, by design (no projection is ever billed); (6) `BnplBillingDatabaseTest`
  lives in `bnpl` over bnpl's JDBC stores and the in-memory book (the `-013` precedent: the real postings are `app`'s),
  the due dates reached by `BnplClockFrame` (lending's `ClockStep`, in a schema of bnpl's own); (7) spans per step
  (`BnplFlowScope`) stay `-026`'s, as `-013` recorded. **Gate** - CRITICAL: none. IMPORTANT (repaired): (1) the last
  instalment's remainder rule was unprobed in its only distinguishing case - with accrued interest at or below the
  projection the amount rule meets the remainder, so removing the rule stayed green; the gate's
  `BnplServicingTest#theLastInstalmentBillsTheRemainderWhateverTheInterest` (accrued interest above the projection) now
  catches it. MINOR: (1) `BnplServicingMetrics` counted with `Counter.increment(double)` - refused by
  `NoFloatingPointMoneyRulesTest` on the first fresh run; one increment per item; (2) the OpenAPI baseline regenerated
  (four additions, all compatible); (3) the first probe runner measured nothing (0 tests - the shell never reached
  gradle, and CRLF anchors failed to match) - no result taken from it, every probe re-run; (4) recorded, not fixed: the
  backlog's first probe (`UNIQUE (instalment_id)` dropped) is unobservable hermetically and probably live too, B4 and the
  ledger key deciding first (`MUTATION_TESTING.md` §2's note); the schedule loop's failing-obligation case has no hermetic
  test (`BnplTransactions` needs a `DataSource`) and is `BnplBillingDatabaseTest#aFailingObligationDoesNotHoldThePage`'s,
  owed. **Multi-instance: `PASS`** - ten instances claim disjoint pages (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, the permit re-stamped
  in the claim); B4 serialises every step on one obligation, the billings, the floor and the catch-up number read after
  it and re-judged under it by the triggers; `UNIQUE (instalment_id)`, `(obligation_id, value_date)`, `(billing_id)`,
  `(obligation_id, catch_up_sequence)` and the ledger keys beneath; every date the database clock's after the lock, the
  due date never early, every application floored; one transaction per step with its outbox row; no JVM state.
  **Probes** (`MUTATION_TESTING.md` §2): twelve caught on hermetic suites, each restore sha256-verified byte-identical; the
  first owed. **Verified** (fresh, `--rerun`): bnpl hermetic **229** (`BnplServicingTest` 20, `BnplServicingMigrationTest`
  6), bnpl architecture **3**, app **133** (the `bnpl` package and the guard suites by name), app architecture **171**
  (the whole tier), all 0 failures. **Written, not run**, owed a first run: `BnplBillingDatabaseTest` (fifteen cases), the
  amended `BnplAcceptanceDatabaseTest`.

**P12-TSK-017 — PN interest accrual** — `COMPLETE` (2026-10-19, gated in Phase 12 wave C beside `-018`; marks no task `READY` - the wave's board rule 9 gives that to `-018`) *(read "`IN_PROGRESS` (started 2026-10-19 …" until its gate)* (`READY` marked by `P12-TSK-015`'s completion gate, 2026-10-18: its one dependency `-015` `COMPLETE`; `-018` depends on `-015` alone and may run beside it)
- **Objective**: a PN obligation earns interest every day, exactly once per obligation and date, on the
  database clock, caught up after any outage — in its own transaction, so the currency's shared
  `BNPL_INTEREST_INCOME` row is never held across a wallet wait (T-acc; the Phase 11 gate's A2-F1 designed
  out).
- **Bounded context**: BNPL; Ledger.
- **Dependencies**: `-015`.
- **Scope**: `bnpl V009`: `bnpl_interest_accrual` (`UNIQUE (obligation_id, accrual_date)`; base, cumulative
  exact, `posted_minor`, period start, agreement version, accrual engine version, entry id — null for a zero
  day; INSERT-only; refused for a P4 obligation, whose terms `CHECK` the rate to zero); **T-acc**
  (`PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §7.1): run by the servicing sweep before T-svc, or first by any act that needs the
  record caught up — **(B4)** the obligation `FOR UPDATE`, the database clock after it; each elapsed date
  `d` (the clock past the end of `d` in the pinned zone, never an instance clock) accrued oldest-first from
  the purchase's business date while principal outstanding at the end of `d` > 0; the base `BNPL_PRINCIPAL +
  BNPL_PRINCIPAL_DUE` over journal lines valued on or before `d` (never interest or fees, never the
  projection); `ACCRUAL_ENGINE_V1` through `creditmath`, built from `AccrualTerms`' canonical constructor (not
  `of(LoanTerms)`), cumulative rounding once per instalment period; F2a `DR BNPL_INTEREST_ACCRUED / CR
  BNPL_INTEREST_INCOME`, key `bnpl.accrual:<obligation>:<date>`, value date `d`, the income row taken at L8
  inside T-acc, which takes no (P); a zero day writes the row and no entry; then commit — **T-acc takes no
  wallet and no payable, and T-svc, T-rep, T-ref, T-pay and the corrections never accrue inside their own
  transaction**: each verifies under B4 that every elapsed date is accrued, else writes nothing and runs
  T-acc first (the door retrying once, never a loop); the floor (`-015`'s function) now includes the latest
  accrual; `-015`'s owner-role accrual fixture replaced by real accruals; scenario 18.
- **Out of scope**: billing (`-015`); interest release on a refund (`-021`); a payoff's projection
  (`-022`); an accrual correction run (none is needed; the key `bnpl.accrual-correction:<obligation>:<date>
  :<engine>` reserved, nothing posted under it).
- **Domain changes**: `BnplInterestAccrual`; `BnplAccruals` (T-acc) and the "caught up" check every act
  calls.
- **Persistence**: `bnpl V009`.
- **APIs**: none — the agreement read shows accrued-to-date interest derived from the ledger.
- **Events**: none — a per-day event is refused (the Phase 11 precedent); `InstalmentDue` carries what
  became due.
- **Policy/model versioning**: each accrual row names the agreement version and the accrual engine version.
- **Financial impact**: F2a, daily — PN interest income recognised as earned.
- **Invariants**: `INV-LND-02`, `INV-LND-09`, `INV-LND-10` (by analogy), `INV-IDEM-02`, `INV-BAL-05`,
  `INV-BNPL-01`.
- **Distributed-system concerns**: **scenario 18** — the accrual run twice, by ten sweepers, restarted
  mid-run and under ±5 s skew → one row and one entry per (obligation, date), never early; a crash between
  dates (each date its own row-and-entry pair, one transaction — neither or both); a scheduler down three
  days → caught up oldest-first; a customer repayment arriving while the record is behind → T-acc first,
  then the repayment against a caught-up base; **the income row**: a servicing step stalled on a held
  wallet holds no `BNPL_INTEREST_INCOME` lock (asserted from `pg_locks`), and T-acc commits past a held
  wallet unblocked. `PASS` on the counts of `BnplAccrualDatabaseTest`.
- **Idempotency**: the born-once row plus the ledger key `bnpl.accrual:<obligation>:<date>`.
- **Consistency**: the base derived from journal lines by value date under B4; the date judged on the
  database clock after the lock.
- **Atomicity**: T-acc is one transaction per catch-up — its rows and entries together; no other act's
  effects inside it.
- **Failure handling**: a failing obligation re-stamps its permit with the retry cadence and does not hold
  the page; a missed day is caught up, never skipped; an act finding the record behind writes nothing and
  answers through T-acc first.
- **Security**: a system act with no door.
- **Audit**: none — a scheduled process's rows and entries are its trail.
- **Observability**: `finapp.bnpl.accrual{outcome}`; `finapp.bnpl.accrual.lag` (seconds since the oldest
  unaccrued elapsed date; alert above one day — the lending precedent, added to `PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §15 by this
  task).
- **Reconciliation implications**: `BNPL_INTEREST_ACCRUED` explained by Σ accruals − Σ billed interest
  (− released, `-021`) — the subledger proof's arm (`-025`).
- **Tests**: `BnplAccrualDatabaseTest` (`#accruesOncePerDate` (**scenario 18** — twice, ten sweepers, a
  restart mid-run), `#skewNeverAccruesEarlyOrTwice`, `#threeMissedDaysAreCaughtUpOldestFirst`,
  `#theBaseIsDerivedFromPostingsNotTheProjection`, `#leapDayAccruesOneDay`, `#zeroDaysWriteARowAndNoEntry`,
  `#aP4ObligationNeverAccrues`, `#anActOnABehindRecordRunsTheAccrualFirst`,
  `#theAccrualHoldsNoWalletAndNoIncomeRowIsHeldAcrossAWalletWait` (lock-wait, `pg_locks`),
  `#aFailingObligationDoesNotHoldThePage`); `BnplBillingDatabaseTest#pnBillsTheAccruedInterestNotTheProjection`
  re-asserted through real accruals.
- **Probe**: drop `UNIQUE (obligation_id, accrual_date)` and the key's date part → `#accruesOncePerDate`
  red; accrue inside T-svc after its wallet lock → `#theAccrualHoldsNoWallet…` red (the income row held
  across the wallet wait); judge the boundary on the instance clock → `#skewNeverAccruesEarlyOrTwice` red.
- **Acceptance criteria**: every elapsed date of every PN obligation accrued exactly once, never early, on
  a principal-only base, in a transaction that holds no wallet or payable.
- **Definition of done**: `DOD-FIN` (F1, F2, F3, F6, F7 binding; F4 vacuous — a correction run is reserved,
  not built, recorded; F5 vacuous — no external event; F8: the subledger proof). **Risk**: High. **Cx**: M.

- **Refined by `P12-TSK-015`** (2026-10-18): `bnpl V008` already creates the accrual RECORD, `bnpl.bnpl_interest_accrual`, in the
  shape above (`UNIQUE (obligation_id, accrual_date)`, base, cumulative exact, `posted_minor`, period start and end, agreement
  version, accrual engine, entry id null for a zero day; INSERT-only, never truncated; its trigger: an `ACTIVE` pay-in-N
  obligation only, never early on the database clock, never before the purchase date, oldest first, never into a billed
  period) with **SELECT only** granted to the application role - so the billing's interest is held to rows for every writer
  from the first billing and `bnpl.principal_value_floor` already has its accrual arm (`max(accrual_date) + 1`). `bnpl V009`
  therefore adds the **writer**: the `INSERT` grant, the agreement/engine checks in the trigger it replaces, T-acc and F2a.
  The "caught up" check `-015` calls is `BnplServicing#accruedThroughTheEve` (the latest accrual on or after the eve) - this
  task refines it for dates with no principal outstanding (which write no row) and moves it to `BnplAccruals`.

- **Refined by `P12-TSK-017` itself** (2026-10-19, at its design, each with its reason):
  1. **The accrual span ends at the final due date.** A date accrues only inside an instalment period of the latest
     schedule version, `[start, D1) … [D(n-1), Dn)` - nothing at or after `Dn`. No billing exists to make post-maturity
     interest due (Phase 12 has no lending-style post-maturity billing), `PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §12.3 admits no penalty
     interest, and `-015`'s gate (`latest accrual >= eve`) would have answered `BEHIND_ACCRUAL` for ever after the final
     due date - the defect this removes. `bnpl V009`'s trigger holds it for every writer. *(Owner judgement: interest on
     principal still unpaid after maturity would need a post-maturity billing - a later task's, never an accrual nobody
     can bill.)*
  2. **"Caught up"** is `BnplAccruals#caughtUp`: no elapsed date of the span with principal outstanding at its end
     unaccrued (a date with none writes no row, so "the latest accrual is the eve" was not the rule); `BnplServicing`
     calls it, `-018`'s T-rep and the later acts will.
  3. **T-acc is bounded**: at most 92 dates a call (lending's `MAX_ACCRUALS_PER_STEP`); the sweep calls it up to 8 times
     before the step (more than any span), and a step that still answers `BEHIND_ACCRUAL` (a midnight between the two
     transactions) has T-acc once more and the step once more - never a loop.
  4. **F2a is posted on the business date**, value-dated `d` - `-015`'s billing convention (lending posted on `d`), so a
     caught-up outage shows when it was recorded.
  5. **The base** is read through a new `BnplBook#datedLinesOn` (ledger's `PurposeBalances#datedLinesOn`, one statement
     under B4) and folded through `Money` - no new ledger API.
  6. **The trigger's added ranks** (beside V008's): B4 re-taken for every writer, the agreement version in force and the
     accrual engine it pins, an instalment period of the latest schedule version, the period's cumulative figure never
     falling; still no ledger read (the subledger proof, `-025`, holds rows to entries).
  7. **The tests' shapes.** `BnplAccrualDatabaseTest#theAccrualHoldsNoWalletAndNoIncomeRowIsHeldAcrossAWalletWait` runs
     over the bnpl suites' in-memory book (the bnpl database suites have no real ledger), so it asserts that a paused
     T-acc holds no lock outside bnpl's relations and that a step on the obligation waits on B4 alone; the real-ledger
     `pg_locks` half has no wallet wait to observe until a T-svc step takes a wallet - owed to `-019`'s collection.
     `#leapDayAccruesOneDay` is hermetic only (`BnplAccrualsTest`): the bnpl database suites purchase on the real date and
     cannot frame a purchase into a leap year; `#zeroDaysWriteARowAndNoEntry` is hermetic for the arithmetic and raw
     writers for the entry `CHECK` in the database suite. `-015`'s hermetic owner-role fixture in `BnplServicingTest`
     stays (billing's reading of whatever the record holds); its database fixture is replaced by real accruals.
  8. **No new scheduler, no event, no door** (as planned); the correction key is reserved as
     `BnplAccruals.CORRECTION_KEY_PREFIX`, nothing posts under it.
- **As built** (2026-10-19, `P12-TSK-017`'s gate): A pay-in-N obligation earns interest every day, exactly once per obligation and date, on the database clock, caught up after any outage, in a transaction of its own that holds no wallet or payable (T-acc). `bnpl V009` adds the writer of `-015`'s `bnpl_interest_accrual` (INSERT granted; the trigger replaced - B4 for every writer, the agreement in force and its engine, an instalment period of the latest schedule version so nothing accrues at or after the final due date, the cumulative chain); `BnplAccruals` accrues every elapsed date of the span with principal outstanding oldest first on `ACCRUAL_ENGINE_V1` over the base `BNPL_PRINCIPAL + BNPL_PRINCIPAL_DUE` folded from journal lines (`BnplBook#datedLinesOn`), F2a `DR BNPL_INTEREST_ACCRUED / CR BNPL_INTEREST_INCOME` under `bnpl.accrual:<obligation>:<date>` at L8, at most 92 dates a call; `BnplServicing`'s gate is `BnplAccruals.caughtUp` (the `-015` gate, which held a matured obligation `BEHIND_ACCRUAL` for ever, replaced); the sweep runs T-acc first (up to 8 calls, once more on a step still behind); meters `finapp.bnpl.accrual{outcome}` and `finapp.bnpl.accrual.lag`. Gate: 14 probes performed, all caught (`MUTATION_TESTING.md` §2); the ten-instance question `PASS`; `BnplAccrualDatabaseTest` (eleven cases) and the re-asserted billing case written, owed a first run. Fresh counts: `:bnpl:test` 252/0 (`BnplAccrualsTest` 14, `BnplAccrualMigrationTest` 4 new), `:bnpl:architectureTest` 3/0, `:app:test` over `com.finapp.app.bnpl.*` and the guard suites by name 189/0 (`BnplAccrualMetricsTest` 2 new), `:app:architectureTest` 171/0. **Owed** (the owner's no-`databaseTest` instruction): every `BnplAccrualDatabaseTest` case and `BnplBillingDatabaseTest#pnBillsTheAccruedInterestNotTheProjection` through real accruals; the real-ledger `pg_locks` income-row assertion to `-019`. **Minor, recorded:** pay-in-4 obligations take one extra B4 transaction a sweep (T-acc answers `NOT_ACCRUING`); a date inside the span with no principal outstanding writes no row, so the lag gauge and `-015`'s billing eve-rank would count it unaccrued - unreachable for an `ACTIVE` obligation in Phase 12 (no not-due principal is prepaid, a refund to zero closes); the currency's `BNPL_INTEREST_INCOME` projection row serialises T-acc commits fleet-wide (the plan's design, one short transaction); `bnpl V009` requires the latest schedule version to start at the purchase's business date - `-021`'s version n+1 must keep it.

**P12-TSK-018 — Customer repayment from the wallet and closure** — `COMPLETE` (2026-10-19, wave C beside `-017`; its gate marks `P12-TSK-019` `READY`) *(read "`IN_PROGRESS`" from its start until its gate)*
- **Objective**: the customer repays any amount from their wallet; it is allocated exactly by the pinned
  order, once, and the obligation closes exactly when every receivable is zero, every elapsed date accrued
  and any credit balance returned (B6: the wallet is the only source).
- **Bounded context**: BNPL; Ledger; Accounts (the wallet, through `app`'s `BnplWallets`).
- **Dependencies**: `-015`.
- **Scope**: `bnpl V010`: `bnpl_repayment` (kind `CUSTOMER` | `AUTO_COLLECTION` | `PAYOFF`; the requester's
  `request_key`, `UNIQUE (obligation_id, kind, request_key)` the arbiter behind a lapsed claim; amount; agreement
  and allocation engine versions; value date; entry by value; no status column — `REVERSED` derived from
  `-024`'s approved reversal; INSERT-only, born only once its money moved), `bnpl_repayment_allocation`
  (ordinal; target `DUE_ITEM` | `CREDIT_BALANCE` — no not-due-principal target: early money is held and applied
  at the next billing; the billing and component exactly when it pays one; amount), a deferred check (Σ rows
  = amount; no billed component over-paid), `bnpl.billing_component_paid` replaced to count allocations beside
  applications, `bnpl_obligation_closure` (`UNIQUE (obligation_id)`; reason; the credit-balance refund and its
  entry `bnpl.closure-refund:<obligation>`; the closing repayment, if any; a deferred check holding it to its
  obligation `CLOSED`) and the obligation's edge `ACTIVE → CLOSED (REPAID)` only beside its closure — `bnpl_repayment`
  and `bnpl_repayment_allocation` **extended** from `-013`'s (born there for P4's instalment 1, T-pur's F3, kind
  `AT_PURCHASE`; reconciled by the transition's consistency pass). T-rep (`PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §7.1): claim `bnpl.repayment:CUSTOMER:<id>`; **(B4)** the obligation
  conditional on `ACTIVE` (else `409 bnpl.ObligationClosed`), the database clock after it; PN caught up (else
  T-acc first, `-017`); the due state derived under B4 (`BnplReceivables`); `ALLOCATION_ENGINE_V1` (oldest
  due first, `FEES → INTEREST → PRINCIPAL`, excess `HOLD_AS_CREDIT`); **(P)** the wallet alone — the
  customer's **existing** `CUSTOMER_WALLET` whatever their standing (`BnplWallets.existingWallet`, never
  opened), `FOR UPDATE`, `AvailableBalance.underLock` ≥ amount; **(L8)** `lockBalancesInOrder`; F3 (`DR
  CUSTOMER_WALLET A / CR <due accounts …> / CR BNPL_CREDIT_BALANCE rest`, lines aggregated per account, the
  per-item split in the allocation rows), key `bnpl.repayment:<repaymentId>`, value-dated `max(today,
  floor)`; closure when settled — the credit balance refunded to the wallet and `CLOSED (REPAID)` in the same
  transaction, through one `BnplClosures` called from **both** zeroing transactions (this repayment, and
  `-015`'s servicing step after an application that settles the obligation); the doors `POST
  /v1/me/bnpl-agreements/{id}/repayments` (the platform's conditional step-up, A18) and `GET
  /v1/me/bnpl-agreements/{id}/repayments`; no standing check (a suspended customer may still repay);
  scenario 6.
- **Out of scope**: auto-collection (`-019`); reversal (`-024`); payoff (`-022`); a refund's closure reasons
  `REFUNDED` / `REFUNDED_PARTIALLY_REPAID` (`-021`); any card-funded or external inbound repayment (B6, A7).
- **Domain changes**: `BnplRepayment`, `BnplRepaymentAllocation`, `BnplClosure`, `BnplClosures`;
  `AllocationAnomaly`.
- **Persistence**: `bnpl V010`.
- **APIs**: the two routes, keyed `bnpl.repayment:CUSTOMER:<id>`; errors `409 bnpl.ObligationClosed`, `422
  bnpl.InsufficientFunds` (absent or not-`ACTIVE` wallet folded in, the Phase 11 precedent) — catalogued in
  `ERROR_CONTRACT.md` by this task.
- **Events**: `InstalmentPaid` (instalment, amounts by component) for each item the allocation settles;
  `BnplAgreementClosed` (reason).
- **Policy/model versioning**: the allocation order and treatment from the pinned agreement version; the
  engine version on the row.
- **Financial impact**: F3 — the customer's own funds settle the claim, any excess owed back; at closure
  the credit balance returned (F6's refund arm). Exposure (v3, `-012`) and capital headroom (`-005`) fall by
  the principal repaid at commit.
- **Invariants**: `INV-BNPL-01`, `INV-LND-04` and `INV-LND-08` by analogy, `INV-IDEM-01`, `INV-CON-01`,
  `INV-BAL-04`, `INV-BAL-05`, `INV-LIFE-04`, `INV-BNPL-10` (exposure and headroom restored at commit).
- **Distributed-system concerns**: **scenario 6** — two repayments concurrently on one instalment →
  serialised on B4, each allocating against what it finds, Σ allocations = Σ amounts, no due account
  negative, never over-allocated; the same repayment twice (one key, two instances) → one repayment, one
  entry, the answer replayed; ten keys on one obligation → serialised and conserved; a repayment racing
  billing on the due date → serialised on B4; a repayment to an obligation closed a moment earlier → `409`,
  nothing posted; a repayment racing a wallet-paid capture by the same customer → the wallet row only, so no
  pair-order question arises (it takes no payable). `PASS` on the counts of `BnplRepaymentDatabaseTest`.
- **Idempotency**: the claim per customer, `UNIQUE (obligation_id, kind, request_key)`, the ledger key
  `bnpl.repayment:<repaymentId>`.
- **Consistency**: the due state under B4, then the available balance under the wallet's lock — the wallet
  always after the obligation (§7.2).
- **Atomicity**: the repayment, its allocations, the entry, the closure, the refund, the events and their
  outbox rows in one transaction.
- **Failure handling**: insufficient funds refused before posting (`422`, nothing written); a closed
  obligation refused (`409`); a record behind its accrual → T-acc first, never a stale base; an unexplained
  ledger (allocation anomaly or the deferred check at commit) refused and metered.
- **Security**: owner-scoped (another party's agreement → `404`); step-up per the platform's conditional
  rule; no amount, party or agreement in a log line, tag or span attribute.
- **Audit**: none — the customer's own repayment is its row and its entry.
- **Observability**: `finapp.bnpl.repayment{kind, outcome}`, `finapp.bnpl.allocation.anomaly` (alert above 0).
- **Reconciliation implications**: internal; the due accounts explained by billings less allocations and
  applications, the credit balance by overpayments less applications less closure refunds — the subledger
  proof's arms (`-025`).
- **Tests**: `BnplRepaymentDatabaseTest` (`#twoRepaymentsSerialiseAndConserve` (**scenario 6**),
  `#theSameRepaymentTwiceRepaysOnce`, `#tenKeysOneObligationConserve`, `#partialLeavesTheRemainderDue`,
  `#overGoesToTheCreditBalanceAndIsAppliedAtTheNextBilling`, `#aRepaymentRacingTheBillingOnTheDueDateConserves`,
  `#theLastRepaymentClosesAndRefunds`, `#aCreditBalanceThatSettlesTheObligationClosesAtServicing`,
  `#anObligationIsNotClosedOverAnUnaccruedDay`, `#aClosedObligationRefuses`, `#insufficientFundsPostsNothing`,
  `#aSuspendedCustomerMayStillRepay`, `#theRepaymentIsFloored`, `#exposureAndHeadroomFallByThePrincipalRepaid`,
  `#theDueStateIsDerivedFromRowsNotTheProjection`, `#repaymentTakesTheObligationThenTheWallet` (lock-wait));
  `BnplRepaymentApiTest` (ownership, step-up); `BnplBillingDatabaseTest#aCreditBalancePaysTheBill`
  re-asserted through a real overpayment.
- **Probe**: take the wallet before the obligation → `40P01` in `#twoRepaymentsSerialiseAndConserve`
  against a racing collection; derive the due state from the projection under a planted projection drift →
  the same test over-allocates, red.
- **Acceptance criteria**: every repayment allocates exactly; no due account ever negative; closure iff
  every receivable is zero and every elapsed date accrued, nothing owed back after it.
- **Definition of done**: `DOD-FIN` (F1, F2, F3, F6, F7 binding; F4 by `-024`, recorded; F5 vacuous —
  wallet repayments are internal and final; F8: the subledger proof), `DOD-API`, `DOD-SEC`. **Risk**: High.
  **Cx**: M.
- **Refined by `P12-TSK-018`'s design (2026-10-19), each with its reason:**
  - **T-rep does not run T-acc first.** The backlog read "PN caught up (else T-acc first, `-017`)". The repayment is
    value-dated `max(today, floor)` and the floor is the day after the latest accrual, so no accrued date's base moves; a
    date not yet accrued later reads a base valued on or before it, which this repayment is not; the allocation pays only
    billed items, which the accrual does not change. Only the closure needs the record caught up, and it judges that
    itself - the next servicing step (T-acc first) closes an obligation the repayment settled over an unaccrued day.
    Requiring T-acc in the customer's door would make it hostage to a sweep for no correctness gain. `-017` agrees (board).
  - **The closure's accrual test is T-acc's own span**: no date from `max(purchase date, latest accrual + 1)` through
    `min(eve, final due date - 1)` with principal outstanding at its end left unaccrued (`-017`: nothing accrues at or
    after the latest schedule version's final due date). With every instalment billed this is implied for pay-in-N (the
    last billing waits on every accrual of its period) - kept as the closure's own defence; since `-017`'s merge it is
    `BnplAccruals.caughtUp`. `#anObligationIsNotClosedOverAnUnaccruedDay` therefore plants the record behind (hermetic); the
    database suite proves a pay-in-N obligation repaid after maturity closes at once (`#aPnRepaidAfterItsFinalDueDateCloses`).
  - **`bnpl.billing_component_paid` is not replaced**: `bnpl V008` already counts the repayments' due-item lines beside
    the applications'; V010 adds the repayment side's own deferred "no component over-paid" check over that definition.
  - **The allocation row keeps `sequence` and `instalment_id`** (`-013`'s V006 columns) for the backlog's "ordinal" and
    "billing": one billing per instalment (`UNIQUE (instalment_id)`), so the instalment names the billed item exactly;
    no `NOT_DUE_PRINCIPAL` target admitted (the CHECK replaced), one line per (instalment, component), one credit line.
  - **No `BnplRepayment` / `BnplRepaymentAllocation` types beside `-013`'s `BnplPurchaseStore.Repayment`/`Allocation`**:
    one row type for every kind (kinds as its constants `CUSTOMER`, `AUTO_COLLECTION`, `PAYOFF`); a parallel domain type
    would be a second copy of one fact. `BnplClosure`, `BnplClosures`, `AllocationAnomaly` (which `BnplReceivables.Anomaly`
    now extends) are new.
  - **`AUTO_COLLECTION` and `PAYOFF` are known to the kind `CHECK` but refused by the trigger** until `-019`/`-022`
    replace it beside their own facts (the attempt, the payoff execution) - so no repayment of those kinds can exist
    without its fact.
  - **`422 bnpl.InsufficientFunds`'s title widened** from "the first instalment" to "the payment" (one code for both
    wallet refusals; `ERROR_CONTRACT.md` and `openapi.json` follow); `409 bnpl.ObligationClosed` added.
  - **T-svc's closure takes (P) after the step's own L8**: the step locks the obligation's six projection rows before
    billing; those rows are written only by holders of B4, so waiting on the wallet while holding them closes no cycle,
    and the wallet's own projection row is taken after (P). Recorded in `DISTRIBUTED_EXECUTION.md` §3.
  - **Events**: `InstalmentPaid` per item a repayment settles (amount and fees/interest/principal paid by it) - not per
    partly-paid item; `BnplAgreementClosed` on the obligation aggregate. No repayment-received event (none planned).
  - **The repayment's view carries no `receivedAt`** (the receipt is the replay; the history is newest-first by it).
- **As built** (2026-10-19, `P12-TSK-018`'s gate): `bnpl V010` (the repayment's kinds and every-writer B4, the allocation's
  `HOLD_AS_CREDIT` target, billed-only rank, per-component uniques and deferred conservation, `bnpl_obligation_closure`
  and the edge beside it); `BnplRepayments` (T-rep), `BnplClosures` (called by T-rep and by `BnplServicing`'s closure step
  after the catch-up), `BnplRepaymentStore`/`JdbcBnplRepaymentStore`, `BnplClosure`, `AllocationAnomaly`;
  `BnplRepaymentController`/`BnplRepaymentDesk`/`BnplRepaymentMetrics`/`BnplRepaymentBeans` in `app`. **Gate**: IMPORTANT
  (fixed in-task) - the closure's first accrual rule (lending's fold through the eve) would have held a pay-in-N obligation
  repaid after its final due date open for ever, `-017`'s span ending there; the closure now asks `BnplAccruals.caughtUp`,
  one rule for every act. MINOR (fixed) - a private row record's default `toString` carried the key and the amount;
  `BnplMigrationTest`'s table and function lists, stale since `-015`'s V008, brought to V010. Thirteen probes performed and
  caught on hermetic suites (`MUTATION_TESTING.md` §2); the wallet-before-obligation `40P01` is `-019`'s to observe (no
  collection races a repayment until then). Ten-instance `PASS`. Owed a first run: `BnplRepaymentDatabaseTest` (twenty
  cases) and `app`'s own-container `BnplRepaymentApiTest` (three, the step-up and the ownership negative).
  **For `-019`**: collect through `BnplRepayments`' posting shape and close through `BnplClosures.closeIfSettled` with the
  wallet you hold under (P) as `walletHeld` (your step's lock), the collection before the closure in T-svc; replace
  `bnpl_repayment_is_born_once` to admit `AUTO_COLLECTION` beside its attempt; add `auto_collection` outcomes to
  `BnplRepaymentMetrics` (its series are eager already).

**P12-TSK-019 — Auto-collection** — `COMPLETE` (2026-10-19, wave D beside `-021`; its gate marks `P12-TSK-020` `READY`) *(read "`READY`" - marked by `P12-TSK-018`'s gate - and "`IN_PROGRESS`" until its gate)*
- **Objective**: what is due is collected from the customer's wallet on the due date — once per instalment
  per day, partially when the pinned terms allow, retried daily while due (A7; B6 — the wallet only, no card
  charge).
- **Bounded context**: BNPL; Accounts (through `app`).
- **Dependencies**: `-018`.
- **Scope**: `bnpl V011`: `bnpl_collection_attempt` (`UNIQUE (instalment_id, attempt_date)`, `UNIQUE
  (repayment_id)`; outcome `COLLECTED` | `PARTIAL` | `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` | `WALLET_NOT_POSTABLE` |
  `NOTHING_DUE`; what the instalment had due, what was collected, the repayment exactly when money moved;
  INSERT-only; a deferred check that every `AUTO_COLLECTION` repayment is named by its attempt at commit);
  T-svc's collection step after billing and the catch-up application (`-015`'s fixed order), under B4:
  per billed instalment oldest first, the instalment's due in full, or — only under partial terms — as much
  as is available; once an instalment is not collected in full nothing younger is collected that day;
  **(P)** the wallet alone (`BnplWallets.existingWallet`, `AvailableBalance.underLock`); a repayment of
  kind `AUTO_COLLECTION` through `-018`'s allocation, entry and closure, the attempt `<instalment>:<date>`
  as its request key, value-dated at the floor rule; a failed attempt posts nothing and tomorrow's is a new
  row; retried at the first step of each later business date while due (a missed date is not back-filled);
  a collection that settles the obligation closes it in its step; `BnplCollectionFailed` when nothing
  could be collected; scenario 4.
- **Out of scope**: any card-funded collection or new system-initiated card charge (B6, `PHASE_12_PLAN.md`
  §20); the dispute hold's effect on collection (`-023` amends this step); delinquency (`-020`).
- **Domain changes**: `BnplCollectionAttempt`, `CollectionOutcome`; the collection step in T-svc.
- **Persistence**: `bnpl V011`.
- **APIs**: none.
- **Events**: `InstalmentPaid` (through `-018`'s allocation), `BnplCollectionFailed` (instalment, outcome).
- **Policy/model versioning**: partial collection on/off from the pinned agreement version.
- **Financial impact**: as `-018` — F3 from the wallet.
- **Invariants**: `INV-IDEM-02`, `INV-LND-04` by analogy, `INV-BAL-04`, `INV-BNPL-01`.
- **Distributed-system concerns**: **scenario 4** — ten sweepers on one due date → one collection; the
  sweep racing a customer repayment (`-018`) and the catch-up application on the due date → serialised on
  B4, never more than due collected; two obligations of one customer collected concurrently → serialised on
  the one wallet row, each bounded by the available balance it finds. `PASS` on the counts of
  `BnplCollectionDatabaseTest`.
- **Idempotency**: the attempt born once per (instalment, date); the repayment's `UNIQUE (obligation_id,
  kind, request_key)` and ledger key.
- **Consistency**: the due state under B4 and the available balance under the wallet's lock, re-derived per
  attempt.
- **Atomicity**: the attempt, any repayment, its allocations, the entry, any closure and the events in one
  transaction step.
- **Failure handling**: insufficient funds or a wallet not postable records the attempt and posts nothing;
  DPD runs from the due date (`-020`); the customer may repay any time (`-018`).
- **Security**: the authority is the agreement's repayment method, accepted with the agreement — no door, no
  operator act; no card instrument reachable from bnpl (`BnplModuleIsolationTest`: no `payments` edge).
- **Audit**: none.
- **Observability**: `finapp.bnpl.collection{outcome}`; a collection's repayment in
  `finapp.bnpl.repayment{kind=auto_collection}`.
- **Reconciliation implications**: internal; as `-018`.
- **Tests**: `BnplCollectionDatabaseTest` (`#tenSweepersCollectOnce` (**scenario 4**, with the sweep racing a
  customer repayment), `#theDueDateCollectsOnceWhateverRaces`, `#partialCollectionWhenAllowed`,
  `#allOrNothingWhenNot`, `#insufficientFundsRecordsAndRetriesTomorrow`, `#aWalletNotPostableIsItsOwnOutcome`,
  `#neverMoreThanDue`, `#aCollectionThatSettlesClosesInItsStep`, `#theOnlySourceIsTheWallet` (no payment
  intent or attempt created), `#twoObligationsOfOneCustomerSerialiseOnTheWallet` (counted)).
- **Probe**: drop `UNIQUE (instalment_id, attempt_date)` → `#tenSweepersCollectOnce` red.
- **Acceptance criteria**: at most one collection per instalment per day, never more than due, from the
  wallet only.
- **Definition of done**: `DOD-FIN` (F3, F6, F7 binding; F1, F2 as `-018`; F4, F5 vacuous — an attempt that
  moves nothing posts nothing, and no external event; F8: internal). **Risk**: Medium. **Cx**: M.
- **Refined by `P12-TSK-019`'s design (2026-10-19), each with its reason:**
  - **The retry cadence is the pinned one.** The backlog read "retried at the first step of each later business date while
    due". The terms pin `collection_retry_days` (`bnpl V002`, A7: "daily" is its default of 1) and the pinned version
    governs (the plan's policy and model versioning), so a past-due instalment is attempted on the first step of a business date at least
    that many days after its latest attempt - daily under every term set activated so far; a missed date is never
    back-filled (the attempt is dated the day it is made, and `bnpl V011`'s trigger refuses an attempt dated before an
    earlier attempt of the same instalment).
  - **The attempt names the instalment and the agreement version.** `UNIQUE (instalment_id, attempt_date)` as the backlog
    says - the instalment, not the billing, is the due item every allocation row already names (one billing per instalment,
    `UNIQUE (instalment_id)`); and `agreement_version`, the version whose pinned terms (auto, partial) governed the attempt,
    so the "partial on/off from the pinned agreement version" rule is a row fact the trigger re-judges.
  - **Oldest first, as lending's rule says it**: once an instalment is not collected in full - or an older one is still due
    and not attempted in this step (the cadence) - every younger candidate that day records `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`: the
    pinned allocation would pay the older one first, so a younger collection could not stay on its own instalment.
    `NOTHING_DUE` is recorded only for an instalment on its due date (settled earlier - a repayment or held credit applied
    at its billing); a past-due instalment with nothing due is not a candidate.
  - **One posting half.** No collection-specific posting: `BnplRepayments.receive` (extracted from T-rep, behaviour
    unchanged) is the L8, the F3 entry, the repayment and allocation rows and `InstalmentPaid` for both the customer's
    repayment and the collection (`-018`'s hand-off); the attempt's natural key `<instalment>:<date>` is the repayment's
    `request_key`, so `UNIQUE (obligation_id, kind, request_key)` is a second arbiter of once per instalment and date.
  - **The step's closure follows the collection with the wallet the collection holds** (`walletHeld`, so the wallet row is
    locked once a step) and names the collection's last repayment as the closing one when a collection moved money.
  - **The lock order in T-svc**: B4 → the obligation's own six projection rows (the step's L8 before billing) → (P) the
    wallet alone → L8 over the entry's rows (re-entrant for the obligation's, the wallet's projection row after (P)) - the
    order `-018` recorded for the closure, now taken by the collection first. No shared income row in T-svc at all (T-acc
    commits alone before it).
  - **Test fixtures collect only when a suite asks.** `BnplTermsFixtures` now pins `autoCollection(false)` (lending's
    `LoanTermsFixtures` precedent), so every suite written before the collection step services exactly as it did; the
    collection suites pin terms that collect. Production terms are the operator's (A7 expects them to collect).
  - **The real-ledger proofs live in `app`.** `bnpl`'s database suites run over an in-memory book behind one lock, which
    has no wallet row lock: `#twoObligationsOfOneCustomerSerialiseOnTheWallet` and `#theOnlySourceIsTheWallet` (no
    payment intent or attempt) are therefore in `app`'s own-container `BnplCollectionLedgerDatabaseTest`, beside the two
    proofs owed to the first collection - `-017`'s (a pay-in-N step waiting at (P) holds no `BNPL_INTEREST_INCOME` row) and
    `-018`'s (a repayment queued behind a collection never `40P01`s). `BnplCollectionDatabaseTest` keeps the rest of the
    backlog's list and `bnpl V011`'s ranks by raw writers.
  - **Meters**: `finapp.bnpl.collection{outcome}` (eager, every outcome); a collection that moved money is one
    `finapp.bnpl.repayment{kind=auto_collection, outcome=repaid}` (`closed` for the one the step's closure followed) and an
    attempt that took nothing from an instalment with something due one `{auto_collection, insufficient_funds}` - lending's
    `LoanServicingMetrics` precedent; `Counter.increment()` once per attempt. No new tag key.
  - **Migration**: `bnpl V011` (the wave D board's reservation; `-021` takes `V012`, `-020` `V013`).
- **As built** (2026-10-19, `P12-TSK-019`'s gate): `bnpl V011` (`bnpl_collection_attempt` and its every-writer trigger, the deferred `bnpl_repayment_auto_collection_has_its_attempt`, the repayment's trigger admitting `AUTO_COLLECTION`); `BnplCollections`, `BnplCollectionAttempt`, `CollectionOutcome`, `BnplCollectionStore`/`JdbcBnplCollectionStore`; `BnplRepayments.receive` (T-rep's posting half, extracted unchanged); `BnplServicing`'s collection slot and `ServicingOutcome.collections`; in `app` the `BnplCollections` bean and `finapp.bnpl.collection{outcome}` with `repayment{kind=auto_collection}` in `BnplServicingMetrics`. **Gate**: IMPORTANT (fixed in-task) - a servicing step's refused conservation (an `AllocationAnomaly` from an application or a collection, or the deferred conservation at commit) reached only `servicing{failed}`, never `finapp.bnpl.allocation.anomaly` (the plan's alert above 0): `BnplServicingMetrics.failed(failure)` now raises it, `BnplServicingScheduleTest#aSweepsAnomalyRaisesTheAlert`; IMPORTANT (fixed) - `-018`'s `BnplRepaymentDatabaseTest#theAllocationsRanksHoldForEveryWriter` expected `V010`'s immediate refusal of a raw `AUTO_COLLECTION` repayment, which `V011` defers to commit - it would have gone red on its first run; it now raws a `PAYOFF`. MINOR (fixed) - `BnplCollectionsTest#theAttemptsShape` asserted a random UUID free of "40" (a flake seen on a run); the design note's `INV-LND-09` reference. Sixteen probes performed and caught on hermetic suites (`MUTATION_TESTING.md` §2). Ten-instance `PASS`. Owed a first run: `BnplCollectionDatabaseTest` (nine cases) and `app`'s own-container `BnplCollectionLedgerDatabaseTest` (four), with the backlog's probe (drop the unique → `#tenSweepersCollectOnce` red) and `-018`'s `40P01` probe (`#aRepaymentRacingACollectionNeverDeadlocks`).
  **For `-020`**: the condition step follows the collection in T-svc (the closure between them); an instalment is past due when billed and unpaid at the end of its due date - the collection attempts are evidence, never the DPD; the late fee's `BNPL_FEE_INCOME` at L8 comes after the wallet the collection already holds, so take it in the fee's own `lockBalancesInOrder` after (P), never before; a collection on the fee's day pays FEES first (the pinned order), so assess before collecting only if the plan says so - it does not (§7.1: collect, close, condition, fee).

**P12-TSK-020 — Delinquency, default and late fees** — `COMPLETE` (2026-10-19, Phase 12 wave E beside `-022`; **M12.6 `CLOSED` at 5 of 5**; marks **`P12-TSK-023`** `READY` - its dependencies `-021` and `-020` `COMPLETE`; frees `P12-TSK-024`, its one dependency) *(read "`READY`" - marked by `P12-TSK-019`'s completion gate - and "`IN_PROGRESS`" until its gate)*
- **Objective**: days past due, buckets, cure and default derived honestly from the rows on the database
  clock and recorded as an append-only history of changes; a configured late fee assessed once per
  instalment on its pinned day, capped (A13, A14; `PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §12.8).
- **Bounded context**: BNPL; Ledger.
- **Dependencies**: `-019`.
- **Scope**: `bnpl V013` (renumbered from the plan's `V012` by the Phase 12 wave D board: `-019` took `V011`, `-021`
  `V012`; Flyway runs `outOfOrder = false`): `bnpl_condition_event` (`UNIQUE (obligation_id, business_date, kind)`; kind
  `DELINQUENCY` | `DEFAULT`; old and new bucket, DPD, the default flag, agreement version; INSERT-only),
  `bnpl_fee_assessment` (`UNIQUE (instalment_id, kind)`; kind `LATE`; amount; agreement version; entry; the
  per-agreement cap judged under B4); T-svc's condition step after collection: an instalment past due when
  billed and unpaid at the end of its due date; DPD = the days from the oldest past-due instalment's due date
  to the current business date (database clock, pinned zone), 0 when nothing is past due — derived, never a
  stored counter; the bucket from the pinned bounds; a row appended only on a change; default at DPD ≥ 90
  (A14, `BnplDefaulted`, the flag) and cleared at cure (`BnplDefaultCleared`); grace delays only the late
  fee, never DPD; a closed obligation skipped; then the late-fee step: once per instalment on the day DPD
  reaches the pinned `late_fee_day` (> grace), capped per agreement — F4 `DR BNPL_FEES_DUE / CR
  BNPL_FEE_INCOME`, key `bnpl.fee:<instalment>:LATE`, the currency's shared `BNPL_FEE_INCOME` row taken at L8
  inside the one sorted `lockBalancesInOrder` call, after any wallet the step took (§7.2 — no income row
  before (P)); tests configure a fee, production none until activation (A13); the customer's agreement read
  shows the condition; **never the merchant** (`-014`'s closed view). **Not built**, each recorded:
  acceleration, default or penalty interest, notifications, bureau reporting, a collections case (Phase 13 —
  bnpl emits the facts), write-off (Phase 14); the dispute hold's suspension of DPD and fees (`-023` amends
  these steps); the late fee's release on a refund-cancelled instalment (`-021`) - *carried here by `P12-TSK-021`,
  which landed first: its refund already releases what `-021` can see (pay-in-N interest) and records a wholly
  cancelled instalment (`bnpl_refund_adjustment.whole`), so this task adds a `late_fee_released_minor` arm to the
  adjustment and F5a's `DR BNPL_FEE_INCOME / CR BNPL_FEES_DUE` line inside T-ref's entry for an assessed fee on a
  wholly cancelled instalment (OQ-14), and `BnplLateFeeDatabaseTest#aCancelledInstalmentsLateFeeIsReleased` (scenario
  17's release half).*
- **Out of scope**: waivers (`-024`); collections operations (Phase 13); write-off and provisioning (Phase
  14).
- **Domain changes**: `BnplDelinquencyState` (derived), `BnplConditionEvent`, `BnplFeeAssessment`; the
  condition and fee steps in T-svc.
- **Persistence**: `bnpl V013` (see Scope).
- **APIs**: the customer's agreement read extended with the condition; no new route, no new error.
- **Events**: `BnplDelinquencyChanged` (old and new bucket, DPD), `BnplDefaulted`, `BnplDefaultCleared`,
  `BnplLateFeeAssessed` (ids, amount) — consumed by the future collections owner (Phase 13).
- **Policy/model versioning**: buckets, default threshold, grace, fee amount, day and cap from the pinned
  agreement version; every condition and assessment row names it.
- **Financial impact**: F4 — contractual fee income; conditions post nothing.
- **Invariants**: `INV-LND-12` by analogy (conditions derived), `INV-LND-08` by analogy (none after closure),
  `INV-IDEM-02`, `INV-HIST-01`, `INV-BNPL-01`.
- **Distributed-system concerns**: **scenario 13** — two condition evaluations or ten sweepers → one row per
  change (the unique, B4); a payoff (`-022`) or a closing repayment during the worker → serialised on B4, no
  condition written after `CLOSED`; a repayment curing between sweeps → the next step records the cure; a
  missed day computed from the dates; midnight under ±5 s skew → the database clock; the fee assessed twice
  or by ten sweepers → one; many obligations assessing in one currency serialise briefly on
  `BNPL_FEE_INCOME`, never while waiting on a wallet (the A2-F1 rule; measured by `P12-TST-001`). `PASS` on
  the counts of `BnplConditionDatabaseTest` and `BnplLateFeeDatabaseTest`.
- **Idempotency**: condition born once per (obligation, business date, kind) and only on a change; the fee
  born once per (instalment, kind) plus `bnpl.fee:<instalment>:LATE`.
- **Consistency**: DPD, bucket and default derived under B4 from billings and allocations; the cap judged
  under B4.
- **Atomicity**: the condition row, any assessment, its entry and the events in T-svc's transaction step.
- **Failure handling**: a missed day computes from current state; a crash re-drives; a cap reached assesses
  nothing; a closed obligation is skipped.
- **Security**: reads owner-scoped (customer) or `BNPL_INVESTIGATE` (operator, `-025`); DPD never in a log
  line, tag or span; no condition reaches a merchant consumer (events carry no merchant-facing credit
  figure, `PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §10).
- **Audit**: none — a derived condition's history and a scheduled fee's row and entry are their trail.
- **Observability**: `finapp.bnpl.delinquency{product, bucket}` and `finapp.bnpl.default{product}` gauges
  (counts, never amounts); `finapp.bnpl.fee{outcome}`.
- **Reconciliation implications**: `BNPL_FEES_DUE` explained by Σ assessed − allocated − released − waived —
  the subledger proof's arm (`-025`); the delinquency report's sums ledger-derived (`-026`).
- **Tests**: `BnplConditionDatabaseTest` (`#noConditionAfterClosure` (**scenario 13**, with a payoff during
  the worker), `#currentToEachBucketAndCure`, `#defaultAtNinetyClearedAtCure`, `#reRunningADayWritesNothing`,
  `#tenSweepersOneConditionChange`, `#aCureBetweenSweepsIsRecordedNotOverwritten`,
  `#aMissedDayComputesFromTheDates`, `#graceDelaysOnlyTheLateFeeNeverDpd`,
  `#theHistoryIsAppendOnlyForEveryRole`); `BnplLateFeeDatabaseTest` (**scenario 17**'s application half:
  `#assessedOnceAtTheLateFeeDay`, `#tenSweepersAssessOnce`, `#theCapHolds`, `#graceDelaysTheFee`,
  `#theFeeIncomeRowIsTakenAfterTheWallet` (lock-wait)) — long histories by date-shifted owner-role fixtures.
- **Probe**: store DPD as a counter incremented per sweep → `#aMissedDayComputesFromTheDates` red; write the
  condition every day instead of on a change → `#reRunningADayWritesNothing` red; drop `UNIQUE (instalment_id,
  kind)` → `#tenSweepersAssessOnce` red.
- **Acceptance criteria**: every condition change recorded exactly once; DPD always the date difference to
  the oldest unpaid due date; no condition on a closed obligation; one late fee per instalment, capped.
- **Definition of done**: `DOD-FIN` (F1, F2, F3, F6, F7 binding; F4 by `-024` (the waiver) and `-021` (the
  release), recorded; F5 vacuous — no external event; F8: the subledger proof). **Risk**: Medium. **Cx**: M.
- **Design** (2026-10-19, `P12-TSK-020`'s Command 1, run straight through on the owner's instruction): the slot is
  `BnplConditions` in T-svc after the closure, under B4, only on an obligation the step did not close - first the
  condition step (`BnplDelinquencyState.derive` over the billed items on the business date of the database clock read
  after B4; a `bnpl_condition_event` per change of bucket or flag; a date with a change recorded not evaluated again),
  then the late-fee step (F4 at L8 over the fees-due row and the currency's `BNPL_FEE_INCOME`, after the collection's
  (P)); the customer's agreement read derives the condition live (`condition`, `BnplConditionView`); T-ref releases the
  late fees of the instalments it cancels whole (OQ-14). **Refinements of this entry, each with its reason:**
  - **(1) The fee by the instalment's OWN age, not by DPD.** The entry read "on the day DPD reaches the pinned
    `late_fee_day`"; DPD is the oldest instalment's age, so it would charge every younger past-due instalment early (on
    instalment 2's day 5 an instalment 3 one day late). Lending's `LateFees` (P11-TSK-025) judges each item by its own
    age; mirrored: `business_date - due_date >= late_fee_day`, a missed day caught up while the instalment still owes
    interest or principal, a settled one never charged.
  - **(2) The test fixtures carry no fee unless a suite pins one** (`BnplTermsFixtures.lateFee(0)`; the condition and
    late-fee suites pin EUR 5.00): `-019`'s auto-collection precedent - the fixture's 5.00 would have changed twelve
    earlier hermetic cases' figures. A13's "tests configure a fee" holds; production terms are the operator's.
  - **(3) The release (OQ-14), its scope and its rank.** Released: the fees still due on every billed instalment whose
    whole unpaid principal the refund cancels, and on every billed instalment when the refund leaves no principal
    unpaid - exactly what is due of its `FEES` now (billed less every payer's and every earlier release), so a paid fee
    is never refunded by a release and nothing is released twice (the Phase 11 gate's R3, designed in: `-024`'s waiver
    is bounded by the same billed-less-settled). A partial cancellation releases nothing. `bnpl V013` records it on the
    adjustment (`late_fee_released_minor`, positive only on a whole `BILLED_UNPAID` row) and the refund (their sum),
    counts it as `FEES` settled in `bnpl.billing_component_paid`, and `bnpl.bnpl_refund_conserves` (replaced) holds at
    commit the sum, no component over-settled, and nothing left due of `FEES` on an instalment cancelled whole. Both
    columns `DEFAULT 0` for `-021`'s writers (which name no release); the commit rank refuses a writer that omits one.
  - **(4) An unpaid late fee keeps its instalment past due**: DPD runs over every component (`FEES`, `INTEREST`,
    `PRINCIPAL`) - lending V020/V021's rule.
  - **(5) Every assessment counts toward the cap, a released one included** - a release frees no room (conservative
    to the customer; lending's sum over assessments).
  - **(6) Scenario 13's "payoff during the worker"**: the payoff is `-022`'s, not built; `BnplConditionDatabaseTest#
    noConditionAfterClosure` races the customer's closing repayment against ten steps instead - the same B4 edge to
    `CLOSED`. *For `-022`*: add the payoff to that race.
  - **(7) `#theFeeIncomeRowIsTakenAfterTheWallet` lives in `app`'s own-container `BnplCollectionLedgerDatabaseTest`**
    (the real ledger's row locks; bnpl's database suites run over the in-memory book behind one lock, `-019`'s
    precedent), beside its hermetic twin `BnplLateFeesTest#theFeeIncomeRowIsTakenAfterTheWallet` (the log's order).
  - **(8) One rank beyond lending's**: a condition row is never dated before a change already recorded (the history in
    date order for every writer).
  - **(9) The cure of an obligation whose every instalment is billed is its closure**: a closed obligation is never
    evaluated, so its last `DEFAULT` row stands as written (the gauges count `ACTIVE` obligations only). Recorded for
    the owner.
  - **(10) Meters**: `finapp.bnpl.fee{outcome}` (`assessed`, `capped`), the two gauges, and `servicing{step =
    condition, outcome = recorded}` (the `step` set the plan opened). No new tag key.
  - **(11) Credit exposure and reporting**: unchanged - `-012`'s exposure counts every obligation's principal whatever
    its condition, and a default posts nothing (A14); the delinquency report is `-026`'s.
- **As built** (2026-10-19): `bnpl V013` - `bnpl_condition_event` (`UNIQUE (obligation_id, business_date, kind)`; its
  every-writer trigger: B4, `ACTIVE`, the agreement version in force, the database clock's business date, never dated
  before a recorded change, DPD (`bnpl.days_past_due`), bucket (`bnpl.delinquency_bucket`) and flag re-derived from the
  rows, only on a change) and `bnpl_fee_assessment` (`UNIQUE (instalment_id, kind)`, `UNIQUE (journal_entry_id)`; its
  trigger: B4, `ACTIVE`, a billed instalment of its own obligation, the version in force, the clock's date, own age >= the
  pinned day, <= the pinned fee, Σ within the cap, still owing interest or principal), both INSERT-only and never
  truncated; `billing_component_billed` (FEES = assessed fees) and `billing_component_paid` (FEES settled by a release)
  replaced; `late_fee_released_minor` on `bnpl_refund_adjustment` and `bnpl_refund`; `bnpl_refund_conserves` replaced.
  `BnplConditions` (the condition step, the late-fee step, the read), `BnplDelinquencyState`, `BnplDelinquencyBucket`,
  `BnplConditionKind`, `BnplConditionEvent`, `BnplFeeKind`, `BnplFeeAssessment`, `BnplConditionStore` /
  `JdbcBnplConditionStore`; `BnplServicing`'s slot after the closure; `ServicingOutcome.conditionChanges/fees/feesCapped`;
  `BnplRefunds`' release (`lateFeesReleased`, F5a's fee lines inside T-ref's one L8 call); `BnplRefund.lateFeeReleased()`.
  In `app`: the beans, `BnplConditionMetrics` (`finapp.bnpl.delinquency{product, bucket}`, `finapp.bnpl.default{product}`),
  `finapp.bnpl.fee{outcome}` and `servicing{condition, recorded}`, the agreement read's `condition` (`BnplConditionView`)
  and the schedule's `billedFees`; `docs/api/openapi.json` (compatible additions only).
- **Gate** (2026-10-19): CRITICAL - none. IMPORTANT - none. MINOR (fixed in-task) - the customer's schedule showed an
  instalment's `due` including its late fee but no field saying what was charged: `BnplScheduledInstalmentView.billedFees`
  (`BnplAgreementDeskTest#theScheduleView` now on a fee-bearing instalment; `openapi.json` one compatible addition). MINOR
  (recorded) - `bnpl V013`'s fee trigger admits a fee below `least(fee, cap room)` (lending V021's parity: the rank is "at
  most"); the domain always assesses the full room. MINOR (recorded) - the release's commit rank ("an instalment cancelled
  whole owes no fee after the refund") has its hermetic and text halves; no raw-writer database case reaches it (a whole
  adjustment needs a refund row of its own obligation), so its live half is the domain refund's path in
  `BnplLateFeeDatabaseTest#aCancelledInstalmentsLateFeeIsReleased`, owed. **Owner judgements** (recorded, not changed):
  (a) a pay-in-N instalment whose principal a partial refund cancels whole while its billed interest stays owed (A11) has
  its fee released, yet may be charged one later if it was not charged before (the interest it still owes is late); (b) a
  released fee frees no cap room; (c) an obligation cured by its closure keeps its last `DEFAULT` row (the gauges count
  `ACTIVE` obligations only). **Seventeen probes performed, all caught on their first run** (`MUTATION_TESTING.md` §2):
  the backlog's first two (DPD a counter; a row every day) and fifteen more - the once-a-day guard, the `ACTIVE` guards of
  the step and the read, the flag held at cure, the once-per-instalment check, the fee by DPD instead of own age, grace for
  the fee day, the cap, the income row before (P), no release, the whole-cancellation arm, a paid fee released again, the
  fee not joined to `FEES` and the release not settled (`V013` text), the fee meter once per step; each restore
  byte-identical, sha256-verified. Owed (database-only, written, not run): the backlog's third probe (`UNIQUE (instalment_id,
  kind)` dropped) and the condition unique's, the live triggers, the income row's real lock order. **Ten-instance `PASS`**:
  B4 serialises every act on an obligation - the sweep's steps, repayments, refunds, payoffs - each reading the history and
  the assessments after the lock on the database clock read after it; `UNIQUE (obligation_id, business_date, kind)`,
  `UNIQUE (instalment_id, kind)` and the ledger key `bnpl.fee:<instalment>:LATE` beneath it; `bnpl V013`'s triggers re-take
  B4 and re-judge DPD, bucket, flag, change, day, fee, cap and owing for every writer; the shared `BNPL_FEE_INCOME` row is
  taken at L8 after any (P) and nothing but inserts follows it, so no step or refund holds it while waiting on a wallet (a
  refund that needs the wallet must first take its `ledger_account` row at (P), which a collecting step already holds);
  DPD is a difference of dates, so skew, missed and repeated sweeps cannot drift it; nothing rests on JVM state or a
  scheduler of its own (`LEASE_PROTECTED_SCHEDULERS` stays 28). Verified, fresh results: bnpl 383 (`BnplConditionsTest`
  12, `BnplLateFeesTest` 17, `BnplDelinquencyStateTest` 3, `BnplConditionMigrationTest` 5), bnpl architecture 3, `app`
  `com.finapp.app.bnpl.*` and the guard suites by name 236 (`BnplConditionMetricsTest` 1, `BnplServicingScheduleTest` 7,
  `BnplAgreementDeskTest` 5), `app` architecture 171 at the end of implementation and 171 again after the gate's fix -
  every one 0 failures; `build`, `databaseTest` and `kafkaTest` not run (the owner's instruction, a criterion-7
  deviation). Owed a first run: `BnplConditionDatabaseTest` (nine cases), `BnplLateFeeDatabaseTest` (six),
  `BnplMigrationTest` through `V013`, and `app`'s own-container `BnplCollectionLedgerDatabaseTest#theFeeIncomeRowIsTakenAfterTheWallet`.
  **For `-022`**: the payoff quote counts `BNPL_FEES_DUE` from the ledger, which now carries late fees - add a payoff with an
  assessed fee (board rule 4), and the payoff to `BnplConditionDatabaseTest#noConditionAfterClosure`'s race. **For
  `-023`**: the dispute hold amends `BnplConditions.evaluate`/`assessLateFees` (no DPD, no fee on a held instalment) and
  the derivation in `bnpl.days_past_due`. **For `-024`**: the waiver subtracts approved waivers in
  `bnpl.billing_component_billed(.., 'FEES')` (lending V021's shape); the release and the waiver are both bounded by billed
  less settled, so neither can forgive what the other already did (the Phase 11 gate's R3).

**P12-TSK-021 — Merchant refunds, latest instalments first** — `COMPLETE` (2026-10-19, Phase 12 wave D beside `-019`, master `9aca4d2c` (`-019`) merged in; marks no task `READY` - the wave's board rule 9 gives that to `-019`; leaves `P12-TSK-022` dependency-free once merged (its other dependency `-017` `COMPLETE`)) *(read "`IN_PROGRESS`" from its start until its gate)*
- **Objective**: a merchant refunds all or part of a BNPL purchase over its own key at any point in the
  instalment lifecycle; the refund cancels unpaid instalments from the last backwards, returns any excess to
  the customer's wallet, takes the merchant fee back pro rata by the cumulative method, and preserves value
  exactly (B3, ADR-0105; gate criteria 1 and 2) — with `INV-MER-07`'s amendment (B7) landing with it.
- **Bounded context**: BNPL (the refund and its adjustment); Merchant (the refund authority, the payable, the
  key scope); Ledger; Accounts (the wallet).
- **Dependencies**: `-009`, `-016`, `-018`.
- **Scope**: `bnpl V012` (*renumbered from the plan's `V013` by the wave D coordinator, 2026-10-19; `-020` takes
  `V013`*): `bnpl_refund` (`UNIQUE (merchant_id, refund_key)`; purchase, amount `R`, fee
  returned, payable debit, principal cancelled unbilled and billed, excess to the customer, the merchant's
  reason (`RESTRICTED-PII`), the merchant key, the entry; born `APPLIED` — a row exists only once its effects
  posted), `bnpl_refund_adjustment` (one row per instalment touched: unbilled or billed principal cancelled;
  late fee and PN interest released), a deferred check (Σ adjustments + excess = `R`) and the purchase's edge
  `FINANCED → FULLY_REFUNDED` when Σ refunds = gross; `bnpl.billing_component_paid` replaced to subtract
  cancellations; the closure trigger admitting `REFUNDED` / `REFUNDED_PARTIALLY_REPAID`; **merchant `V011`**
  (the next free after `-006`'s `V010`, unless `-006` placed it — said so): the merchant key's refund scope —
  a key carries it only when issued with it (ADR-0052's issuance door extended); keys issued before carry none,
  failing closed. **T-ref** (`PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §7.1): claim `bnpl.refund:MERCHANT:<id>` (merchant key,
  refund scope); **(B5)** the purchase `FOR UPDATE` — the refund bound's arbiter — `R ≤ G − refunded` else
  `422 bnpl.RefundExceedsPurchase`, a fully refunded purchase `409 bnpl.PurchaseFullyRefunded`, another
  merchant's purchase `404`; **(B4)** the obligation, the database clock after it; PN caught up (else T-acc
  first); the split by `-009`'s pure allocator over the due state derived under B4 — from the last
  instalment back, `min(remaining R, unpaid principal)` each (unbilled → `CR BNPL_PRINCIPAL`; billed-unpaid
  → `CR BNPL_PRINCIPAL_DUE`, curing its DPD; a partly paid instalment cancels only its unpaid part); excess
  `E` to the customer's wallet (A12) — or held in `BNPL_CREDIT_BALANCE` when the wallet cannot be credited,
  refunded at closure or when postable (OQ-13); the fee returned `cum_fee(after) − cum_fee(before)`,
  telescoping to exactly `f` at a full refund (§12.5); late fees on a cancelled instalment released (OQ-14 — `-020`'s
  assessments; `-020` is not among this task's dependencies, so if this task lands first the release arm and
  scenario 17's release half are carried to `-020`, said so);
  PN: principal reduced latest-first by `ScheduleEngineV1.recalculateAtInstalment` (same instalment, least
  term), accrued and billed interest staying owed except at a full cancellation, which releases it (A11);
  schedule v n+1 and agreement v n+1 whenever an unbilled instalment is cancelled or shortened (`INV-HIST-04`);
  **(P)** the merchant's `MERCHANT_PAYABLE` and — when `E > 0` — the customer's `CUSTOMER_WALLET` rows `FOR
  UPDATE` as one pair in `UUID.compareTo` order of the two account ids (payments' `lockPairInFixedOrder`
  order, §7.3 (b)); **(L8)** `lockBalancesInOrder` with the currency's `BNPL_MERCHANT_FEE_INCOME` (and,
  when released, `BNPL_FEE_INCOME`, `BNPL_INTEREST_INCOME`) inside the one sorted call; F5 + F5a in one entry
  (`DR MERCHANT_PAYABLE R; DR BNPL_MERCHANT_FEE_INCOME r_f / CR BNPL_PRINCIPAL; CR BNPL_PRINCIPAL_DUE; CR
  CUSTOMER_WALLET E; CR MERCHANT_PAYABLE r_f`, the releases beside them), key `bnpl.refund:<refund>`,
  value-dated at the floor rule; the refund and adjustment rows; closure if every receivable is now zero
