- **Refinements of the backlog, with reasons**: (1) **the refund's unique is `(merchant_id, requested_by, refund_key)`**,
  not `(merchant_id, refund_key)` - the operator's door keys per operator (`OPERATOR:<identity>`), and two operators, or an
  operator and the merchant, are distinct requesters; at the merchant's door it is the same rule. (2) **Schedule version
  n+1 is a whole schedule** (the billed instalments carried as new rows, their billed principal and interest; the
  unbilled tail as the refund left it), so `V009`'s periods and the billing's period and principal rules hold unchanged;
  **"billed" is therefore judged by due date** (one billing per due date, `UNIQUE (obligation_id, value_date)`) in the
  billing's oldest-first rank, the closure's every-instalment-billed rank, `BnplServicing.dueUnbilled` and
  `BnplClosures` - the billings keep naming version n's instalment. (3) **Pay-in-N's adjustment rows are the allocator's
  latest-first split, not "the difference between schedule v n and v n+1"** (plan §12.6 point 5): an annuity re-amortised
  at the same instalment shifts every remaining instalment's principal - earlier ones up, later ones down or gone - so a
  per-instalment difference is not a cancellation; the identity held at the database rank is the version's, `principal(v
  n+1) = principal(v n) - the unbilled principal cancelled`, so the principal still to bill falls by exactly the split's
  unbilled total (the proof `P12-TSK-009` carried here). (4) **Pay-in-N interest accrued is released also when the refund
  leaves nothing more to bill** (the whole unbilled tail cancelled, billed principal still owed): no instalment remains
  to make that accrued interest due, so it could never be billed and the obligation could never close; A11's "stays owed"
  holds for every refund that leaves an unbilled instalment - recorded for the owner. (5) **An empty schedule version is
  admitted** (a pay-in-N refund of every unit of principal before the first billing): `instalment_count 0`, principal 0;
  the accrual span is then empty. (6) **The closure's reason**: `REFUNDED` whenever the purchase is `FULLY_REFUNDED` -
  also when a later servicing step refunds a credit balance the refund held (OQ-13); `REFUNDED_PARTIALLY_REPAID` only in
  a partial refund's own transaction; `REPAID` otherwise (`BNPL_LIFECYCLES.md` §4.7, read with OQ-13). (7) **The operator
  door** - the plan named none (OQ-9): `POST /v1/operator/bnpl-purchases/{id}/refunds` under `PAYMENT_REFUND`, the ADR's
  default (the payments refund's one permission, held by `LEDGER_OPERATOR`), keyed per operator (`bnpl.refund:<actor type>:<id>` - `CUSTOMER`-typed for an operator session today, the platform's known debt), the
  reason audited, an operator of the purchase's own party refused `403 bnpl.SelfDealingRefused` and recorded `FAILED`.
  (8) **The 403 is `bnpl.RefundScopeRequired`** (the backlog's "`403` for a key without the scope", the ADR's "merchant's
  key-scope refusals"): judged at bnpl's door, recorded `FAILED` (`bnpl.RefundScopeRefused`). (9) **The scope is issued
  by a query parameter** - `POST /v1/operator/merchants/{id}/api-keys?scope=BNPL_REFUND` - not a body: the issuance door
  takes no body, and a required one would refuse every existing issuance. (10) **`409 bnpl.RefundNotPostable`** (new):
  a refund of a `CLOSED` agreement whose wallet cannot take it (OQ-15's refusal), or a payable that cannot be debited -
  nothing written, the merchant retries under the same key. (11) **The wallet is never opened** (ADR-0105 decision 2.2
  said "resolved or opened"): bnpl's `BnplWallets` answers the existing wallet only; an absent or unpostable one holds
  the excess as credit (an `ACTIVE` obligation) or refuses (a `CLOSED` one). (12) **The merchant's view** shows each
  refund's id, amount, fee returned, payable debit, instant and door, and the merchant's own reason only for a
  merchant-door refund (an operator's reason is the operator's record); "partially refunded" derived. (13) **The kind
  meter** counts after the transaction: `applied`, `closed`, `exceeds_purchase`, `fully_refunded`, `not_postable`,
  `self_dealing_refused`; the scope refusal is its audit record. (14) **Carried**: the late fee's release (OQ-14) and
  `BnplLateFeeDatabaseTest`'s release half to `-020` (above); `409 bnpl.DisputeOpen` to `-023` (no dispute table yet);
  ADR-0105's open question on `AccountClosing`'s pending-credits port - not built: a closed wallet makes the excess held
  (or, after closure, the refund refused), which is safe - recorded for the owner.

- **Refinements of the backlog, with reasons**: (1) **the quote is read plainly, not under (B6)** - it is INSERT-only
  (an `UPDATE`-less role cannot take `FOR UPDATE` on it, and nothing could change under the lock); the execution's
  `UNIQUE (quote_id)` and `UNIQUE (obligation_id)` beneath B4 arbitrate, lending's `P11-TSK-026` shape. (2) **The payoff's
  value date `V = max(G, floor)` is fixed once, on the execution row, from the floor read before any write**, and
  `principal_value_floor` counts a payoff's billings at most at `V`: an early billing keeps its row dated its due date
  (so "billed" stays judged by due date, `-021`'s rule, and the closure's and the billing trigger's ranks hold unchanged)
  while its entry is valued `V` - so the floor can never climb to a future due date inside the payoff, and every
  application, the repayment and the early entries land on `V`, never before the floor (RG-M1) and never in the future.
  (3) **An instalment already due but not yet billed** (the servicing step not yet run today) is billed in the payoff
  exactly as T-svc bills it, its entry valued its due date - one billing rule, base-neutral either way. (4) **A payoff
  makes no schedule or agreement version** (the plan's §5.4; lending's shape) - the backlog was silent. (5) **The quote
  is refused, not computed, on a record behind its accrual**: the backlog said "after T-acc's catch-up"; the desk runs
  T-acc in its own transaction and asks again, as `-021`'s refund door does, so neither act holds the currency's income
  row (A2-F1). (6) **The projection stops at the accrual span's end** (`projected_days` may be fewer than `G - today`):
  T-acc accrues nothing at or after the final due date (`-017`). (7) **Fees**: `BNPL_FEES_DUE` is counted from the ledger
  generically, and the `PAYOFF` repayment allocates it through `BnplReceivables`' due state - whatever model `-020` gives
  a late fee must keep that due state explaining the account, as every repayment already requires. (8) **The execution
  also refuses a moved agreement version or engine** before recomputing (`AMOUNT_CHANGED`), and a held credit beside a
  receivable after the applications is an `AllocationAnomaly`, never a gross debit with a refund beside it.
  (9) **Lending's RG-M1 is not remediated here** (board rule 10): bnpl floors its own payoff; the recommendation that
  lending's payoff applications be floored alike stays open.

**P12-TSK-023 — BNPL disputes** — `COMPLETE` (2026-10-19, Phase 12 wave F beside `P12-TSK-024`, branch `P12-TSK-023`, bnpl `V015`; **M12.7 at 3 of 4**; marks no task `READY` - the wave's board rule 11 gives that to `-024`) *(read "`READY`" - marked by `P12-TSK-020`'s completion gate, its dependencies `-021` and `-020` `COMPLETE` - and "`IN_PROGRESS`" until its gate)*
- **Objective**: a customer contests a BNPL purchase with the platform (there is no card network on it); the
  disputed amount is held — no late fee, no DPD, no collection on it — until the merchant accepts, the
  deadline passes, the customer withdraws or an operator resolves; a refund outcome *is* a refund under the
  same bound, so a dispute and a refund can never double-credit (`INV-BNPL-08`, ADR-0106; gate criterion 3).
- **Bounded context**: BNPL (the dispute, the hold); Merchant (the response, over its key); `app`.
- **Dependencies**: `-021`, `-020`.
- **Scope**: `bnpl V015`: `bnpl_dispute` (+ `_event`; reason (`RESTRICTED-PII`), disputed amount ≤ gross −
  refunded at opening, the response deadline (14 days, OQ-10 — a pinned terms field), the outcome, the
  resolving refund; partial `UNIQUE (purchase_id)` over `OPEN`, `MERCHANT_RESPONDED`; the machine's edge
  trigger and status `CHECK` — `PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §5.8: `OPEN → MERCHANT_RESPONDED → RESOLVED_REFUND |
  RESOLVED_UPHELD`, `OPEN → RESOLVED_REFUND` (merchant accepts, or the deadline passes — silence is
  acceptance), `OPEN | MERCHANT_RESPONDED → WITHDRAWN`); **the hold**: while open, the instalments a refund of
  the disputed amount would cancel — latest first, the same walk as `-021`'s allocator, so a refund outcome
  cancels exactly what was held — are suspended: `-019`'s collection step skips them, `-020`'s condition step
  excludes them from DPD and its fee step assesses no late fee on them (both steps' functions replaced, each
  its predecessor plus only the hold); **T-dsp** (`PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §7.1): claim; **(B5)** the purchase;
  **(B4)** the obligation; **(B6)** the dispute `FOR UPDATE` conditional on its from-state; on
  `RESOLVED_REFUND` → T-ref's body (`BnplRefunds`, `-021`) in the same transaction for `min(disputed, G −
  refunded)` judged under B5, so a merchant refund that came first leaves the dispute's refund only what
  remains (possibly zero — resolved with nothing to refund, recorded); `RESOLVED_UPHELD` lifts the hold and
  re-bills nothing (nothing was cancelled); `BnplDisputeSchedule` (leaderless; disputes past their deadline →
  `RESOLVED_REFUND`, the deadline the permit) — `LEASE_PROTECTED_SCHEDULERS` +1 (29 with `-011`'s and `-015`'s);
  the doors `POST /v1/me/bnpl-agreements/{id}/disputes` (customer, keyed `bnpl.dispute:CUSTOMER:<id>`), the
  customer's withdrawal (its route this task's design — `PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §9 names none), `POST
  /v1/merchant/bnpl-disputes/{id}/response` (merchant key; evidence or acceptance; `bnpl.dispute-response:
  MERCHANT:<id>`), `POST /v1/operator/bnpl-disputes/{id}/resolution` (`BNPL_DISPUTE_RESOLVE`, four-eyes above
  the threshold — a pinned terms field, its place this task's design since the plan names none;
  `bnpl.servicing:EMPLOYEE:<id>`); scenario 10. **Cut order**: the operator resolution is the phase's first
  cut (`PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §16) — merchant-accepted and deadline refunds kept.
- **Out of scope**: chargebacks on the financed amount (none can exist — no network, §12.7); a payments
  dispute on a card-funded wallet top-up (payments', unrelated to the agreement); merchant credit risk; a
  dispute evidence store beyond the response text (ADR-0061's evidence regime is payments').
- **Domain changes**: `BnplDispute` and its machine; `DisputeHold` (derived from the open dispute); the
  collection, condition and fee steps aware of it.
- **Persistence**: `bnpl V015`.
- **APIs**: the four doors; errors `409 bnpl.DisputeOpen` (a second open dispute), a `409` for an act on a
  dispute not in its from-state (named by this task), `422 bnpl.ReasonRequired`, `403 bnpl.SelfApprovalRefused`,
  `403 bnpl.SelfDealingRefused`, `404 bnpl.NotFound` — catalogued in `ERROR_CONTRACT.md` by this task.
- **Events**: `BnplDisputeOpened`, `BnplDisputeResolved` (outcome); `BnplRefundApplied` on a refund outcome.
- **Policy/model versioning**: the response window and the four-eyes threshold from the pinned agreement
  version; the refund outcome priced by the purchase's fee pin.
- **Financial impact**: F9 = F5 — a refund outcome under the same bound; an upheld or withdrawn dispute posts
  nothing.
- **Invariants**: `INV-BNPL-08`, `INV-BNPL-07`, `INV-BNPL-06`, `INV-LIFE-01`…`-04` (the machine), `INV-AUD-04`,
  `INV-HIST-01`, `INV-MER-01`.
- **Distributed-system concerns**: **scenario 10** — a dispute's refund outcome racing a merchant refund on
  one purchase → serialised on B5, at most `G` returned across both, never double-credited; one open dispute
  per purchase under two instances (the partial unique); the deadline sweep on two instances and a merchant's
  late acceptance at the deadline → exactly one `RESOLVED_REFUND` (the conditional edge on the database clock);
  ten operator resolutions → one; a collection racing the dispute's opening → serialised on B4, never
  collecting a held instalment after the open commits. `PASS` on the counts of `BnplDisputeDatabaseTest`.
- **Idempotency**: keyed doors per actor; the machine's conditional edges; the refund outcome's own refund
  key (`bnpl.refund:<refund>`) and the shared bound.
- **Consistency**: the bound under B5; the hold and the due state under B4.
- **Atomicity**: the dispute's edge, the hold's effect, any refund, its entry, the events, outbox rows and
  audit rows in one transaction.
- **Failure handling**: the merchant's silence resolves by the sweep at the deadline; a resolution finding
  the purchase fully refunded resolves with nothing to refund; a crash re-drives from rows.
- **Security**: customer owner-scoped (MFA per the platform's conditional rule); merchant key and tenant
  isolation on the response; `BNPL_DISPUTE_RESOLVE`, four-eyes above the threshold (domain and `CHECK`),
  never one's own act; an employee never resolves a dispute of their own party; the merchant never sees the
  customer's schedule or condition; reasons screened and `RESTRICTED-PII`.
- **Audit**: `bnpl.DisputeOpened`, `bnpl.DisputeResponded`, `bnpl.DisputeResolved`, and every self-approval
  and self-dealing refusal recorded `FAILED` in its own transaction after the rollback (the Phase 11 gate's R4
  applied forward) — catalogued in `AUDITABLE_ACTIONS.md` by this task.
- **Observability**: `finapp.bnpl.dispute{outcome}`, `finapp.bnpl.dispute.sweeper.enabled`.
- **Reconciliation implications**: a refund outcome is in the three-way proof's refund identities; the hold
  is a condition, not a balance — nothing to reconcile.
- **Tests**: `BnplDisputeDatabaseTest` (`#disputeRefundAndMerchantRefundShareOneBound` (**scenario 10**, both
  orders, counted), `#oneOpenDisputePerPurchase`, `#theHoldSuspendsCollectionDpdAndFees`,
  `#theHoldCoversTheLatestInstalments`, `#merchantSilenceResolvesAsARefundAtTheDeadline`,
  `#aLateAcceptanceAtTheDeadlineResolvesOnce`, `#upheldLiftsTheHoldAndReBillsNothing`,
  `#aWithdrawalLiftsTheHold`, `#tenResolversOneResolution`, `#selfApprovalRefusedAtBothRanksAndAudited`,
  `#anEmployeeNeverResolvesTheirOwnPartysDispute`, `#aResolutionAfterAFullRefundRefundsNothing`,
  `#disputeTakesThePurchaseThenTheObligation` (lock-wait B5 → B4)); `BnplDisputeApiTest` (the route register's
  negatives for all four doors); `NoSingleInstanceAssumptionRulesTest` (+1).
- **Probe**: skip the purchase lock in the dispute's refund → `#disputeRefundAndMerchantRefundShareOneBound`
  red (more than `G` returned); collect a held instalment → `#theHoldSuspendsCollectionDpdAndFees` red; drop
  the four-eyes `CHECK` → the raw-SQL self-approval accepted, `#selfApprovalRefusedAtBothRanksAndAudited` red.
- **Acceptance criteria**: at most `G` ever returned to the customer side across refunds and dispute
  outcomes; no late fee, DPD or collection on a held instalment; every resolution four-eyes where required,
  audited.
- **Definition of done**: `DOD-FIN` (F1, F2, F3, F6, F7 binding; F4: the refund outcome is `-021`'s
  compensation, an upheld dispute posts nothing; F5 vacuous — no external event (no network); F8: the
  three-way proof), `DOD-SEC`, `DOD-API`. **Risk**: High. **Cx**: L.

  board, rule 3). Code: `BnplDisputes` (T-dsp), `BnplDispute`, `BnplDisputeProposal`, `BnplDisputeHold`, `BnplDisputeReason`,
  `BnplDisputeStore` / `JdbcBnplDisputeStore`; `BnplRefunds.heldBy` (the allocator as a dry run) and `forDispute` (T-ref's body,
  door `DISPUTE`), its new `DisputeOpen` refusal; `BnplRefund.Door.DISPUTE`; `BnplPurchaseStore.disputeHold`,
  `BnplRefundStore.disputeOpen`; `BnplDelinquencyState.derive(..., hold)`, `BnplConditions` and `BnplCollections` reading the hold
  (constructors unchanged); `BnplErrorCode` +2 (`DisputeOpen`, `DisputeNotActionable`), `BnplAuditAction` +7. `app`:
  `BnplDisputeController` (`POST /v1/me/bnpl-agreements/{id}/disputes`, `POST /v1/me/bnpl-disputes/{id}/withdrawal`),
  `BnplMerchantDisputeController` (`GET /v1/merchant/bnpl-disputes`, `POST /v1/merchant/bnpl-disputes/{id}/response`),
  `BnplOperatorDisputeController` (`GET /v1/operator/bnpl-disputes/{id}`, `POST …/resolution`, `…/resolution/approval`,
  `…/resolution/rejection`, all `BNPL_DISPUTE_RESOLVE`), `BnplDisputeDesk`, `BnplDisputeMetrics` (`finapp.bnpl.dispute{outcome}`),
  `BnplDisputeSchedule` (the 29th lease-protected scheduler, `finapp.bnpl.dispute.sweeper.enabled`), `BnplDisputeBeans`;
  `BnplRefundDesk` answering `409 bnpl.DisputeOpen` (`finapp.bnpl.refund{outcome=dispute_open}`); `MerchantBeans`' close port
  asking `anyOpenAtMerchant`; `openapi.json` regenerated (571 lines added, none changed). **Refinements, each for its reason:**
  (1) **the hold is the dispute's own rows by due date**, not `bnpl_condition_event` kinds (ADR-0106 decision 3 read that
  way; `BNPL_LIFECYCLES.md` §8 (d)): that table's once-per-date unique and derivation trigger are delinquency's; due dates are
  stable across schedule versions where instalment ids are not; (2) **an instalment touched by the dry run is held whole** -
  no collection, DPD or fee on it - the backlog's "the instalments … are suspended" (the ADR's "only the undisputed due
  amounts" would split an instalment the allocation engine pays whole); (3) **every lift restarts the clock** - after any
  resolution a held instalment's DPD and fee day count from the later of its due date and the lift's business date (the ADR
  says so for uphold and withdrawal; after a refund outcome only a partly held instalment remains, and it is treated alike);
  (4) **`RESOLVED_REFUND` refunds exactly `D` and always names its refund**: refunds are refused while a dispute is open
  (ADR-0106 decision 7), so `G - refunded` cannot shrink between the opening and the resolution - the backlog's
  `min(disputed, G - refunded)` and "resolved with nothing to refund" are unreachable, and
  `#aResolutionAfterAFullRefundRefundsNothing` proves the reachable case (a fully refunded purchase takes no dispute); (5)
  **four-eyes is a proposal row** (`bnpl_dispute_proposal`, `D >` the pinned threshold): the operator's `…/resolution` above
  it proposes, `…/approval` by another holder of `BNPL_DISPUTE_RESOLVE` executes, `…/rejection` by any (the proposer's
  withdrawal included) clears it - each decision naming its `proposalId`; (6) **the withdrawal's route** is
  `POST /v1/me/bnpl-disputes/{id}/withdrawal`, keyed `bnpl.dispute-withdrawal:CUSTOMER:<id>`, and it is audited
  (`bnpl.DisputeWithdrawn`); (7) **the merchant's response needs its key, not the refund scope** (ADR-0106 decision 4 names
  the key and tenant isolation only); `CONTEST` or `ACCEPT`, a statement required either way (`RESTRICTED-PII`, screened); (8)
  **the merchant close (ADR-0106 decision 11) is built**: the opening takes the merchant's payable alone `FOR UPDATE` at (P)
  and refuses a closed one (`409 bnpl.RefundNotPostable`); the close's settled-payable port asks the open disputes under the
  same row lock - a close and an opening are ordered, never beside each other; (9) **the merchant reads its open disputes**
  (`GET /v1/merchant/bnpl-disputes` - amount, category, deadline, status; never the reason) and **the operator's read is
  audited** (`bnpl.DisputeRead`); (10) **payoff and voluntary repayment are not paused** (the customer's own acts; what they
  pay on held instalments returns as excess on a refund outcome); a dispute on a `CLOSED` obligation holds nothing and its
  refund outcome pays the wallet only (OQ-15); (11) the dispute events carry ids, status, category, the deadline as epoch
  milliseconds (the payload alphabet admits no instant) and the held sequences - never an amount or a text. **Owed a first
  run** (the owner's instruction): bnpl's `BnplDisputeDatabaseTest` (thirteen cases - the backlog's thirteen), `BnplMigrationTest`'s lists through
  `V015`, and `app`'s own-container `BnplDisputeApiTest` (six - the ownership negatives `OwnershipIsScopedTest` names).
- **Gate** (2026-10-19): IMPORTANT (fixed in-task, found by review and proven red first) - a held **older** instalment captured a younger one's auto-collection: the pinned order pays the oldest due first, so a pay-in-N obligation whose instalment 2 owed interest only (a refund had cancelled its principal) while instalment 1 was held made every servicing step an `AllocationAnomaly` - billing, conditions and fees stopped with it; the collection now allocates over the due state with the held instalments taken out (`BnplDisputesTest#aHeldOlderInstalmentNeverCapturesAYoungerOnesCollection`, red before the fix). MINOR (fixed) - a probe survived its first run (the opening's own bound against `G - refunded`: the dry run's allocator refused as a second rank); `#theBoundOnAClosedObligation` (nothing held) now catches it. MINOR (fixed) - `MutationDemonstrationTest` refused a register row whose invariant column read "`INV-LND-11` by analogy". MINOR (recorded) - the merchant's door judges the deadline on the database clock read after B6 and the trigger re-judges it on `clock_timestamp()` microseconds later: an answer landing in that gap is the trigger's refusal (a 500), not `409 bnpl.DisputeNotActionable` - nothing is written either way. **Board rule 12** - every `CHECK`, trigger and unique on the tables written read against the new writes: `bnpl_refund` (its born-once trigger - `FINANCED`, the gross and B7 bounds, the versions in force, the floor, a `CLOSED` obligation's wallet-only arm - met by the `DISPUTE` door unchanged; the door and requester `CHECK`s replaced; `UNIQUE (merchant_id, requested_by, refund_key)` keyed by the dispute's id; the deferred conservation), `bnpl_refund_adjustment`, `bnpl_schedule` / `bnpl_agreement` version n+1 (`refund_id` `UNIQUE`), `purchase`'s `FULLY_REFUNDED` edge, the closure's `REFUNDED` reasons (no door read), `bnpl_collection_attempt` and `bnpl_fee_assessment` (only rows they already admitted are refused), `bnpl_condition_event` (its trigger reads the replaced `days_past_due`, unchanged with no dispute), and the money floor (`BnplSchemaHasNoMutableMoneyTest` - the reason the dispute row is money-free). Twenty-one probes performed - twenty caught on their first run, one after the test above; restores sha256-verified (`MUTATION_TESTING.md` §2). **Ten-instance `PASS`**: B5 orders every dispute act and every refund of a purchase, so the bound, the open-dispute refusal and the one-open rule are judged under it (the partial unique beneath); B4 orders the opening's dry run against collection, servicing, repayment, payoff and accrual - each reads the hold under its own B4; B6 orders the merchant's answer, the deadline sweep, the withdrawal and the operator's acts, the deadline's complementary conditionals on the database clock after the lock and the edge trigger's re-judgement making exactly one win; the proposal's partial unique and its four-eyes `CHECK`; one refund per dispute by `UNIQUE (dispute_id)` and the ledger key; the opening's (P) on the payable orders it against the merchant close; the sweep's claim commits alone and holds no row; nothing rests on JVM state. Verified on the merge (master `81f7cf97`, already merged), fresh results: bnpl 450 tests in 41 suites (`BnplDisputesTest` 28, `BnplDisputeHoldTest` 4, `BnplDisputeMigrationTest` 6), bnpl architecture 3, `app` `com.finapp.app.bnpl.*` and the guard suites by name 258 in 47 suites (`BnplDisputeDeskTest` 4, `BnplDisputeScheduleTest` 3; `MutationDemonstrationTest` 9 re-run after its register row was corrected), `app` architecture 171 at the end of implementation and 171 again after the gate's fix - every one 0 failures; `build`, `databaseTest` and `kafkaTest` not run (the owner's instruction, a criterion-7 deviation). **Owed a first run**: `BnplDisputeDatabaseTest` (thirteen), `BnplMigrationTest`'s lists, `app`'s own-container `BnplDisputeApiTest` (six). **Open for the owner**: a dispute against a merchant closed before it is refused (`409 bnpl.RefundNotPostable`) - the customer's contest then has no platform path (a loss-absorbing outcome is a product decision); payoff and voluntary repayment are not paused by an open dispute (recorded, ADR-0106's as-built note). **For `-024`**: `V015` replaces `bnpl.days_past_due` only - V016's `billing_component_billed`/`_paid` are read by it unchanged; a repayment reversal on a held instalment needs no dispute handling (the hold reads billed less settled). **For `-025`**: a dispute's refund is a `bnpl_refund` of door `DISPUTE` - the three-way proof's refund identities count it with the others.

**P12-TSK-024 — Repayment reversal and fee waiver (four-eyes)** — `COMPLETE` (2026-10-19, Phase 12 wave F beside `-023`, master `5aef9eac` (`-023`) merged in; **M12.7 `CLOSED` at 4 of 4**; marks **`P12-TSK-025`** `READY` at its merge-in - its dependencies `-021`, `-022`, `-023` and `-024` `COMPLETE` (board rule 11)) *(read "`PLANNED`" until its start and "`IN_PROGRESS`" until its gate)*
- **Objective**: an operator's mistake in applying a customer's money is undone by an exact reversal, and a
  late fee is forgone only by a bounded waiver — each reasoned, four-eyes and posted, never an edit
  (ADR-0099's shape applied to bnpl).
- **Bounded context**: BNPL; Ledger; Credit (L0, through `BnplCreditDecisions.lockExposure`); Lending's
  capital row (L6, through `BnplCapital`).
- **Dependencies**: `-020`.
- **Scope**: `bnpl V016`: `bnpl_repayment_reversal` (a money-free machine row — the amount is the
  repayment's; `PROPOSED → APPROVED | REJECTED`; four-eyes `CHECK`; `APPROVED` exactly when it names F8's
  entry; one live proposal per repayment — partial `UNIQUE (repayment_id)` over `PROPOSED`, `APPROVED`; the
  reason bounded and screened, `RESTRICTED-PII`), `bnpl_repayment_allocation_reversal` (INSERT-only negating
  rows, one per allocation, whole at commit), `bnpl_waiver` (+ decision; kind `FEE`; target assessment;
  amount; reason; four-eyes `CHECK`), and `bnpl.billing_component_paid` replaced to subtract the negating rows;
  **T-rev** (`PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §7.1): claim `bnpl.servicing:EMPLOYEE:<id>`; **(L0)** the profile (outstanding
  rises — `INV-CRD-09`, `INV-BNPL-10`); **(B4)** the obligation conditional on `ACTIVE` (a closing repayment's
  reversal refused — the Phase 11 A12 shape — `409 bnpl.ObligationClosed`); **(B6)** the proposal conditional
  on `PROPOSED`; **(L6)** `LENDING_CAPITAL` when principal is re-instated, headroom re-checked (`422
  bnpl.CapitalUnavailable`, nothing posted, the proposal still `PROPOSED`); **(P)** the wallet the original
  debited (read from its entry); **(L8)**; `ReversalService` of F3's entry (F8, the exact swap, key
  `bnpl.repayment-reversal:<id>`, bounded by the original — `INV-REV-02`) and the negating rows; later
  allocations not re-cut — the reversed amount simply becomes due again, DPD recomputed by the next step;
  refused for a repayment whose held credit has since been applied (the swap would drive
  `BNPL_CREDIT_BALANCE` below zero — a `409` named by this task, the Phase 11 `RepaymentNotReversible`
  precedent, absent from `PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §9's list); **T-wvr**: claim; (B4); (B6) the proposal; (L8) the
  currency's `BNPL_FEE_INCOME` row (no wallet is taken — after (P)'s position by construction); F7 — a fee
  waiver reverses the assessment's entry through `ReversalService` for the unpaid remainder only, bounded by
  `least(billed − paid, assessed − waived − released − refunded)` (the Phase 11 gate's R3 applied forward:
  what was already released or refunded is never forgiven twice), `422 bnpl.WaiverExceedsDue` beyond it; a
  waiver zeroing the last receivable closes the obligation; the doors `POST
  /v1/operator/bnpl-agreements/{id}/waivers` and `…/repayments/{rid}/reversal` (+ `/approval`, `/rejection`)
  under `BNPL_SERVICE` / `BNPL_SERVICE_APPROVE`, each decision naming the proposal it decides; scenario 12.
- **Out of scope**: an interest waiver (`PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §12.11 has no such rule — recorded, raised at the
  design if wanted); reversal of P4's at-purchase collection beyond the same rule (it is an ordinary
  repayment and reversible while `ACTIVE`); the operator's agreement read and explanation (`-025`).
- **Domain changes**: `BnplRepaymentReversal`, `BnplWaiver` and their proposal machines; the derived
  `REVERSED` status.
- **Persistence**: `bnpl V016`.
- **APIs**: propose, approve and reject for both, keyed `bnpl.servicing:EMPLOYEE:<id>`; errors `403
  bnpl.SelfApprovalRefused`, `403 bnpl.SelfDealingRefused`, `422 bnpl.ReasonRequired`, `409 bnpl.ProposalPending`,
  `422 bnpl.WaiverExceedsDue`, `422 bnpl.CapitalUnavailable`, `409 bnpl.ObligationClosed` and the new
  not-reversible `409` — catalogued in `ERROR_CONTRACT.md` by this task.
- **Events**: `BnplRepaymentReversed`, `BnplFeeWaived` (ids, amounts).
- **Policy/model versioning**: the reversal names the original's agreement version; nothing is recomputed.
- **Financial impact**: F8 — the original's credits debited back, the wallet credited, exactly; F7 — fee
  income forgone, the claim released.
- **Invariants**: `INV-REV-01`, `INV-REV-02`, `INV-REV-04`, `INV-AUD-04`, `INV-HIST-01`, `INV-CRD-09`,
  `INV-LND-13` (re-instated principal under L6), `INV-BNPL-10`, `INV-LND-11` by analogy.
- **Distributed-system concerns**: **scenario 12** — a reversal after allocation (and after later repayments
  and billings) reopens exactly what it paid, later allocations untouched; ten approvers → one reversal; two
  proposals for one repayment → one live; an approval racing a new repayment → serialised on B4; reversals
  racing BNPL acceptances, loan acceptances and draws for the last capital → serialised on L6, never
  over-deployed; a waiver racing a repayment of the fee → bounded under B4, refused or exact. `PASS` on the
  counts of `BnplRepaymentReversalDatabaseTest` and `BnplWaiverDatabaseTest`.
- **Idempotency**: keyed per employee; the proposals' conditional edges; the ledger reversal key and the
  reversal bound.
- **Consistency**: L0 first, then B4, B6, L6, (P), L8; the due state re-derived under B4 and headroom under
  L6.
- **Atomicity**: the approval, the reversal or waiver entry, the negating rows, any closure, the event, the
  outbox row and the audit row in one transaction.
- **Failure handling**: a wallet not postable → the approval refused, nothing posted, the proposal still
  `PROPOSED`; a capital shortfall → `422`, the same; a waiver beyond the bound → `422`, the same.
- **Security**: `BNPL_SERVICE` proposes, `BNPL_SERVICE_APPROVE` approves — never one's own (domain and
  `CHECK`); never one's own party's agreement (`403 bnpl.SelfDealingRefused`); reasons required and
  screened; `RoutePermissionRegisterTest` with negatives.
- **Audit**: `bnpl.RepaymentReversalProposed` / `…Approved` / `…Rejected`, `bnpl.WaiverProposed` /
  `…Approved` / `…Rejected`; every self-approval and self-dealing refusal recorded `FAILED` in its own
  transaction (R4 applied forward) — catalogued in `AUDITABLE_ACTIONS.md` by this task.
- **Observability**: `finapp.bnpl.reversal{outcome}`, `finapp.bnpl.waiver{outcome}`.
- **Reconciliation implications**: the subledger proof includes reversals (allocated − reversed) and waivers
  (assessed − allocated − released − waived); the original entry byte-identical after.
- **Tests**: `BnplRepaymentReversalDatabaseTest` (`#aReversalReopensWhatItPaid` (**scenario 12**),
  `#tenApproversOneReversal`, `#oneLiveProposalPerRepayment`, `#selfApprovalRefusedAtBothRanksAndAudited`,
  `#anEmployeeNeverServicesTheirOwnPartysAgreement`, `#aClosingRepaymentIsNotReversible`,
  `#aRepaymentWhoseHeldCreditWasAppliedIsNotReversible`, `#theOriginalIsByteIdenticalAfter`,
  `#reversalTakesTheProfileFirst` (lock-wait L0), `#exposureRisesByThePrincipalReopened`,
  `#aReversalNeverOverDeploysCapital` (counted against acceptances and draws)); `BnplWaiverDatabaseTest`
  (`#aFeeWaiverReversesOnlyTheUnpaidRemainder`, `#aReleasedOrRefundedFeeIsNeverWaivedAgain` (R3),
  `#tenApproversOneWaiver`, `#waiverRacingARepaymentOfTheFee`, `#aWaiverOfTheLastReceivableCloses`,
  `#theWaiverTakesTheIncomeRowLast` (lock-wait)); `BnplServicingApiTest` (the route register's negatives).
- **Probe**: drop the four-eyes `CHECK` → `#selfApprovalRefusedAtBothRanksAndAudited` red; re-cut later
  allocations instead of reopening → `#aReversalReopensWhatItPaid` red; skip L6 →
  `#aReversalNeverOverDeploysCapital` red; drop the R3 arm of the bound → `#aReleasedOrRefundedFeeIsNeverWaivedAgain`
  red (`BNPL_FEE_INCOME` negative for the obligation).
- **Acceptance criteria**: every reversal exact, four-eyes and reasoned; every waiver bounded; history
  untouched; the subledger proof zero after either.
- **Definition of done**: `DOD-FIN` (F1, F2, F3, F4, F6, F7 binding; F5 vacuous — no external event; F8: the
  subledger proof), `DOD-SEC`. **Risk**: Medium. **Cx**: M.
- **As built** (2026-10-19): `bnpl V016` - `bnpl_repayment_reversal` (money-free machine, column-scoped decision, four-eyes `CHECK`, `APPROVED` exactly beside F8's entry and its value date, partial `UNIQUE (repayment_id)` over `PROPOSED`/`APPROVED`, its edge trigger re-taking B4: an `ACTIVE` obligation, the repayment its own under its agreement version, never `PAYOFF`, the value date between the floor and the later of today and it), `bnpl_repayment_allocation_reversal` (INSERT-only, mirroring, `UNIQUE (allocation_id)`, whole at commit), `bnpl_waiver` + `bnpl_waiver_decision` (INSERT-only; the decision born once, `UNIQUE (waiver_id)`, the proposer copied and pinned for the four-eyes `CHECK`), `bnpl.fee_waiver_room` (both arms of the bound, read by both waiver triggers), and `bnpl.billing_component_billed` / `_paid` replaced (FEES less approved waivers; settled less the negating rows - V013's every other term kept). Code: `BnplRepaymentReversals` (T-rev), `BnplWaivers` (T-wvr), `BnplCorrectionStore`/`JdbcBnplCorrectionStore`, `BnplRepaymentReversal`, `BnplWaiver`, `BnplCorrectionStatus`, `BnplWaiverKind`, `BnplBook` + `reverse`/`entryLines` (`LedgerBnplBook` over `ReversalService` and `JournalEntryStore`), `BnplErrorCode` + 4, `BnplAuditAction` + 6; `app`: `BnplCorrectionController` (the six doors), `BnplCorrectionDesk`, `BnplCorrectionMetrics` (`finapp.bnpl.reversal{outcome}`, `finapp.bnpl.waiver{outcome}`), `BnplCorrectionBeans`, the customer's repayment history's derived `REVERSED`. **Refinements, each for its reason:** (1) the key is `bnpl.servicing:<actor type>:<id>` - operator sessions are CUSTOMER-typed today (`BNPL_LIFECYCLES.md` §7, `-004`'s settled point); (2) **a `PAYOFF` repayment** is refused twice - its obligation is always `CLOSED` (`ObligationClosed`), and the domain and the trigger refuse the kind (`RepaymentNotReversible`) whatever the state - `-022`'s hand-off; (3) **a `CLOSED` obligation is terminal** - lending's A12: the closing repayment and every repayment of a closed obligation are never reversed (reopening a closed agreement would move an obligation out of `CLOSED`, `INV-LIFE-04`); a standing proposal may still be rejected; (4) **the money returns to the wallet F3 debited** (the plan's F8 credits it), so no balance can be short; a wallet that cannot be credited is a new `409 bnpl.WalletUnavailable` (lending's), nothing posted, the proposal still `PROPOSED`; (5) the not-reversible `409` is `bnpl.RepaymentNotReversible` and a decision of a decided proposal `409 bnpl.ProposalNotPending` (both lending's), both new; `bnpl.SelfDealingRefused`'s title widened to agreements; (6) **the value date is `max(today, floor)`** with the floor read under B4 (the repayment's rule), re-judged by the trigger: no accrued date's base moves; the days between the repayment and its reversal accrue on the reduced base and are not recomputed (ADR-0099 point 4, lending's A10); (7) **L0 always** on the approval (lending's), **L6 only when principal is re-instated**; (8) **self-dealing fails closed** - an operator the platform cannot place in a party is refused (lending's `LoanSelfDealing`; `-021`'s refund door is permissive - an owner judgement); (9) **the waiver's (P)**: the backlog's "no wallet is taken" holds when no credit balance stands; beside one, a waiver that zeroes the last receivable refunds it at closure, so the wallet is taken at (P) BEFORE the one L8 call that holds the shared `BNPL_FEE_INCOME` row (the A2-F1 rule) - else the closure would take it after; (10) **the R3 arm** - `least(billed - settled, assessed - waived - released)`; "refunded" in bnpl is the refund's release (no fee-refund kind exists). In V016's sums the second arm is implied by the first (billed - settled = assessed - waived - released - net payments, never negative), so the domain judges it FIRST, from the assessment's own rows, as the belt over a later change to either sum - the probes record what each arm alone catches; (11) the reversal row also carries `value_date` (for the floor rank and `-025`'s replay); (12) `bnpl_fee_assessment` gains `UNIQUE (id, obligation_id, instalment_id)` for the waiver's composite key. **For `-025`**: the explanation lists reversals (`reversalsOf`) and waivers (`waiversOfObligation`); the subledger proof's `BNPL_FEES_DUE = assessed - allocated + negated - released - waived` and `BNPL_PRINCIPAL_DUE` ± reversals; **after a reversal the obligation may hold credit beside a past-due item until the next servicing step's catch-up application** - the replay's RG-M5 arm must judge it at a STEP's end only; a reversed repayment's instalment may draw a late fee at the next step (the payment never happened) - waivable. **For `-023`**: a waiver or reversal on a disputed obligation is not refused (no hold on corrections) - owner judgement.

**P12-TSK-025 — The BNPL proofs and the explanation door** — `COMPLETE` (2026-10-20, branch `P12-TSK-025`, alone - no wave; **M12.8 at 1 of 2**; marks **`P12-TSK-026`** `READY` - its one dependency `-025` `COMPLETE`) *(read "`IN_PROGRESS` (started 2026-10-19 …)" until its gate, "`READY` (marked by `P12-TSK-024`'s merge-in, 2026-10-19: its dependencies `-021`, `-022`, `-023` and `-024` `COMPLETE`; M12.8's first)" until its start, and "`PLANNED`" before)*
- **Objective**: every purchase's figures are continuously proven three ways — merchant leg, customer leg,
  ledger — re-derivable from its pinned agreement and engines, and explainable from rows alone (gate criterion
  5; `PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §12.12).
- **Bounded context**: BNPL; Merchant (the payable, read); Ledger; `app`.
- **Dependencies**: `-021`, `-022`, `-023`, `-024` (and every built servicing task).
- **Scope**: `BnplThreeWayProof` per currency in one `REPEATABLE READ` read-only snapshot: (1) **merchant
  leg** — Σ over purchases (gross − fee) − Σ refunds' payable debits = Σ BNPL lines on `MERCHANT_PAYABLE`
  (by entry id), per merchant, and each payable still satisfying `INV-MER-02`'s equation with the BNPL terms
  (`-016`); (2) **customer leg** — `BnplSubledgerProof` per obligation: `BNPL_PRINCIPAL` = G − billed −
  cancelled-unbilled; `BNPL_PRINCIPAL_DUE` = billed − allocated − applied − cancelled-billed (± reversals);
  `BNPL_INTEREST_ACCRUED` = Σ accruals − billed − released; `BNPL_INTEREST_DUE` = billed − allocated −
  released; `BNPL_FEES_DUE` = assessed − allocated − released − waived; `BNPL_CREDIT_BALANCE` = overpayments
  + held excess − applications − closure refunds; no due account negative; a `CLOSED` obligation all zero;
  (3) **economic identity** per purchase — `G = principal repaid + principal cancelled by refunds +
  principal outstanding`, `Σ refunds = Σ principal cancelled + Σ excess`, fee recognised − fee returned =
  `BNPL_MERCHANT_FEE_INCOME`'s BNPL lines for it; (4) the trial balance zero per currency;
  `BnplReplayProof` (`BnplReplayer` — the pinned engines by version over each agreement and schedule version
  and the ledger's history: schedules, accruals' `posted_minor`, billings, allocations, refund adjustments,
  re-verifying `terms_sha256`; `IDENTICAL` or `DIVERGED`) with **two arms the Phase 11 gate taught**: a
  principal fact valued before its floor → `DIVERGED` (R1's arm), and held credit standing beside a past-due
  item at a step's end → `DIVERGED` (RG-M5 — the "catch-up application expected" check lending lacks, applied
  forward); the capital proof's BNPL term (`-005`) and the exposure census (`-012`) read in the same snapshot
  for the gauges; `BnplBooksHaveOnePosterTest` asserting non-vacuously; `GET /v1/operator/bnpl-agreements/{id}`
  and `/explanation` (`BNPL_INVESTIGATE`, audited: agreement versions and hashes, schedule versions, the
  purchase, the financing, accruals, billings, applications, repayments, allocations, collection attempts,
  refunds and adjustments, disputes, conditions, fees, waivers, reversals, the payoff and every journal entry
  — from rows alone) and `POST …/replay` (`BNPL_INVESTIGATE`, audited, `IDENTICAL` / `DIVERGED`).

  adjustment or an agreement → `DIVERGED`; a raw-SQL posting to a BNPL account without a bnpl row → the
  subledger proof red; a raw posting to a merchant payable under a `bnpl.` key without a purchase → the
  three-way proof's merchant leg red; a raw projection edit → the proof still green (it reads journal lines);
  a planted pre-floor repayment → `DIVERGED`; planted held credit beside a past-due item → `DIVERGED`;
  `#aProofDuringServicingIsStable`, `#theExplanationIsCompleteFromRows`, `#everyClosedObligationIsZero`,

  self-dealing, audit).

  binding; F8: this is the internal reconciliation), `DOD-OBS`. **Risk**: Medium. **Cx**: L.
- **As built** (2026-10-20): no migration (`bnpl V017` stays free). bnpl: `BnplRecord` (an obligation's whole record from rows - purchase, financing, offer and its terms, every agreement and schedule version, billings, accruals, applications, repayments with their allocations, collection attempts, refunds with their adjustments, fees, conditions, quotes, the execution, disputes, reversals with their negating rows, waivers, the closure - and its six accounts' journal lines, the shared entries, the merchant payable and fee income lines; every fact carrying its database stamp) read by `BnplRecordStore` (`JdbcBnplRecordStore`, raw SQL over the bnpl tables and the existing stores, the ledger through `BnplBook`'s dated lines - never `ledger.account_balance`); `BnplSubledgerProof` (the six identities as the entry gives them, reversals and waivers included as `-024` handed over, every entry on an obligation's six accounts named by a row - `namedEntries` - no due account negative, a `CLOSED` obligation all zero, fee income never negative, R3); `BnplReplayer` (the pinned engines by NAME - `BnplEngine`'s pay-in-4 schedule and refund allocation, `creditmath`'s schedule, accrual and allocation - an exhaustive `switch` per version, `EngineAbsent` for a name the build does not hold); `BnplReplayProof` (one walk over the record's facts in database-stamp order: the offer's illustration and `terms_sha256` re-rendered from the offer's rows, every agreement version and schedule version re-projected, every accrual's `posted_minor` and chain on the base as of its writing and again on the final ledger (R1's accrual arm), every elapsed date accrued, every billing's components, every allocation by the pinned order over the due state as of its writing, every credit application and the APPLICATION_MISSING arm at a billing (R2), every principal fact valued at or after the floor as it stood (R1), held credit beside a past-due item judged at a servicing step's later slots only (RG-M5 - `-024`'s hand-off), every refund re-derived through `BnplRefunds.derive` and the pinned refund allocator with its next schedule, every late fee, waiver, reversal, the payoff quote (balances and the projection, by the accrual engine) and execution, the closure; `IDENTICAL` or `DIVERGED` with the finding kinds); `BnplThreeWayProof` (per currency: the merchant leg per merchant - Σ (G − f) − Σ (R − r_f) equal to the `bnpl.`-keyed lines on `MERCHANT_PAYABLE` by entry id, every such entry named by a financing or refund, the payable's `INV-MER-02` equation holding with the BNPL terms; the customer leg - every obligation's subledger verdict; the economic identity per purchase - principal, refunds, fee income and the fee arm (f and every r_f recomputed under the purchase's pin by `BnplMerchants.returnedFee`, `-006`'s hand-off); the trial balance, the capital proof and the exposure census through the `BnplProofReads` port, in the same snapshot); `BnplProofs` (one reading - refuses any connection but a read-only `REPEATABLE READ` one); `BnplExplanations` (the read, the explanation and the replay, the read and the explanation in the caller's `REPEATABLE READ` transaction with their `bnpl.AgreementRead` / `bnpl.ExplanationRead` row appended to it, the replay on a read-only snapshot and `bnpl.Replayed` with its reason in a transaction of its own - counts and verdicts only, never an amount; self-dealing judged first through `BnplRepaymentReversals.judgeSelfDealing`, fail closed, recorded `FAILED`); `BnplRefunds.nextSchedule` made a pure static the replay shares. app: `LedgerBnplProofReads` (`StatementDerivation` over `bnpl.financing:`, `bnpl.refund:` and the catch-all `bnpl.`, `MerchantPayable.payablesOf`, `TrialBalance`, `LendingCapitalProof`, `ExposureCensus`); `BnplProofMetrics` (`finapp.bnpl.threeway.proof{verdict}`, `.subledger.proof{verdict}`, `.replay{verdict}`, eager, one reading behind a refresh floor of 15 minutes, never under 60 s, NaN when unreadable, CRITICAL lines with counts only); `BnplInvestigationDesk` and `BnplInvestigationController` - `GET /v1/operator/bnpl-agreements/{id}` (`investigateBnplAgreement`), `GET …/{id}/explanation` (`explainBnplAgreement`), `POST …/{id}/replay` (`replayBnplAgreement`, a required reason), all `BNPL_INVESTIGATE`, the uniform `404 bnpl.NotFound`, `403 bnpl.SelfDealingRefused`; `BnplProofBeans`. Registers: three routes, three audit actions, OpenAPI regenerated (compatible additions only), `BnplReplayRequest` in the credential-sink register, `JdbcBnplRecordStore`'s reads classified `ADMINISTERED`; `BnplBooksHaveOnePosterTest` gains `theProofsSeeEveryWriter` (non-vacuous over the hermetic world) and `MerchantPayable` as a reader permit.
- **Refinements to this entry, decided by its design and recorded** (2026-10-20): (1) **`BnplProofDatabaseTest` is `app`'s**, an own-container suite: the merchant leg and the ledger arms need the real ledger, merchant and lending modules, which `bnpl` does not see; the hermetic proof suites are `bnpl`'s over `BnplApplicationFakes`; (2) **the ledger-side arms enter through a port** `BnplProofReads` (the payable's keyed lines and equation, the trial balance, capital, the census) - bnpl names none of ledger's, merchant's or lending's types; (3) **the merchant leg's namespaces include the catch-all `bnpl.`** beside `bnpl.financing:` and `bnpl.refund:`, so a raw payable posting under any other `bnpl.` key is an unnamed entry, never unseen; (4) **the capital proof and the exposure census are arms of the three-way verdict**, not separate gauges - the entry's "read in the same snapshot for the gauges" (one gauge, `FAILS` naming the arm in its CRITICAL line); (5) **the facts are ordered by their database stamps** (`created_at`, `billed_at`, `received_at`, `decided_at`, `executed_at` - no `recorded_order` column exists), a refund's schedule and agreement version n+1 applied at the refund itself; a stepped-back database clock between two facts of one obligation could read as a false `DIVERGED` (recorded as debt, alerting, never silent); (6) **RG-M5 is judged at a step's later slots** (its collection attempts, condition events and late fees), never between steps, as `-024` handed over - a step that writes nothing after its catch-up leaves the judgement unobservable (recorded); (7) **the agreement read is a door of its own** (`GET …/{id}`, `bnpl.AgreementRead` - the versions, hashes and schedule versions; the explanation the whole record), and its operation id is `investigateBnplAgreement` (the customer door holds `readBnplAgreement`); (8) **`BnplRefunds.nextSchedule` is a pure static** the replay calls - one re-amortisation, never a copy; (9) **`MerchantPayable` is a reader permit of `BnplBooksHaveOnePosterTest`** - the test had been red since `-016` read the payable's BNPL lines there (found by this task, fixed); (10) collection attempt rows and condition events are listed by the explanation but not re-derived by the replay (their inputs are wallet answers and day counts the derivations of `-019`/`-020` already pin; recorded).
- **For `-026`**: the three gauges exist and are eager (`finapp.bnpl.threeway.proof{verdict}`, `.subledger.proof{verdict}`, `.replay{verdict}`); their alert rules (`FAILS` > 0, `DIVERGED` > 0, absent) and the runbook's reading of a CRITICAL line (arm and kind counts - the obligation found through the audited explanation door, never a log) are `-026`'s; a reading reads every obligation's whole record - one statement per bnpl table per obligation behind the 15-minute floor - so the portfolio's growth is the reading's cost (recorded as debt).

**P12-TST-001 — The BNPL storm** — `PLANNED`
- **Objective**: prove BNPL correct under N instances, clock skew, provider faults and crashes, end to end
  from checkout to closure for both products, beside lending on shared parties, merchants and capital —
  every mandatory scenario exercised, every census at every round, every named lock wait counted, and the hot
  rows measured, not only proven.
- **Bounded context**: all of the phase, with checkout, merchant, payments, settlement, credit and lending as
  they meet it.
- **Dependencies**: every task `P12-TSK-001`…`-026`; **and** the cross-cutting `X-TSK` (not yet numbered)
  that repairs the three settlement suites red since `P9-TSK-026` — `BatchAcceptanceDatabaseTest`,
  `FileReceptionDatabaseTest`, `ReadmissionDatabaseTest` (owner decision B8, OQ-20: fixed before this storm,
  whose scenario 5 runs through merchant payouts and settlement).
- **Scope**: `PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §13.3. **First, the test-hardening debt** recorded by the Phase 11 → 12
  transition, paid before this storm reuses the lending storm's shape (the debt row's own trigger): A6-03 —
  closure censuses judged by the record's order or the clock's step, never a 5 s tolerance, and probed; A6-04
  — every `app` BNPL suite date-shifted from its first run (and lending's app suites, the debt's subject,
  shifted or their exemption recorded); A6-06 — default and bucket coverage forced by the seeded calendar,
  never dependent on today's date; A6-07 — scenario 14's relay kill placed after the receive it must follow;
  each fixed in the shared harness or recorded with why it cannot reach the BNPL world. **Then the storm**:
  two application instances, clocks ±5 s; parties holding loans, lines and BNPL obligations at once; merchants
  shared across captures, BNPL financings and payouts; checkout sessions raced by a BNPL acceptance and a card
  or wallet confirmation; capital contested across lending acceptances, draws and BNPL acceptances (L6);
  refunds (partial, full, after payout, after closure), disputes (merchant acceptance, silence to the deadline,
  operator resolution), payoffs, collections, reversals and waivers racing; merchant payouts with lost
  responses (scenario 5's merchant variant) and **scenario 5's wallet variant** — the customer tops up by card
  through payments' existing pay-in for an instalment, the response lost, the retry under the same key
  replayed, the inquiry concluding once, the instalment then collected once; a BNPL terms activation
  mid-storm; ≥ 3 real business-date boundaries (fixed-offset zones per cohort); **every one of the eighteen
  scenarios** of `PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §13.2; crash points incl. two killed backends and a crash at every T-pur
  step. **At rest, every round**, in one `REPEATABLE READ` snapshot (the Phase 11 lesson I2 — no census at the
  final rest only): the three-way proof zero; the subledger proof zero per obligation; replay `IDENTICAL` per
  obligation; the capital proof with the BNPL term; the exposure census (v3); the trial balance zero per
  currency; one financing per purchase, one purchase and one order per session; Σ refunds ≤ gross per
  purchase and Σ refunds + dispute refunds ≤ gross (`INV-BNPL-08`); every accrual date once; Σ allocations =
  Σ repayments; every payable's `INV-MER-02` equation, every negative payable within its purchases' B7 bound;
  one payout per key at the provider and **dispatches equal on both sides**; every act counted against its
  rows, its audit rows and its meters over the whole run (the C19 lesson — not a window); every gauge zero.
  **Every named lock wait counted** (the M3 lesson), each observed as the act's own backend waiting (the C17
  method): L0, B3, B5, B4, L6 and (P) in both `UUID` orders. **Measured, not only proven** (`PHASE_12_PLAN.md`
  §21; owner item #21; A2-F1): lock-wait counts and wait-time distribution per round on the currency's
  `LENDING_CAPITAL` row and on the shared `BNPL_MERCHANT_FEE_INCOME`, `BNPL_FEE_INCOME` and
  `BNPL_INTEREST_INCOME` rows — recorded as the hot-row characterisation; the pass condition is no deadlock, no
  lock timeout and no income row held across a wallet wait. No figure in its logs (the C1 lesson: every
  obligation, purchase, merchant and party id and every rendered amount searched as whole tokens); the
  must-refuse acts (self-approval, self-dealing, a key without the refund scope) judged by a refusal helper —
  a `2xx` is a failure; the storm seeded and its seed printed.
- **Out of scope**: production volume (the gate's criteria are correctness, §1.1); the fleet-wide
  `databaseTest` and `kafkaTest` tiers (owner decision B4 — the standing criterion-7 deviation).
- **Domain changes**: none — tests.
- **Persistence**: none.
- **APIs**: exercised, none added.
- **Events**: exercised — the outbox census: every state change's event exactly once.
- **Policy/model versioning**: a terms activation mid-storm — the pinned versions decide; replay `IDENTICAL`
  across it.
- **Financial impact**: proof only.
- **Invariants**: every `INV-BNPL-*`, `INV-MER-02`, `INV-MER-05`, `INV-MER-07` (amended), `INV-LND-13`,
  `INV-CRD-09`, `INV-IDEM-01`, `INV-IDEM-02`, `INV-PAY-04`, `INV-SET-06`, `INV-LED-01`.
- **Distributed-system concerns**: the purpose — `PASS` = every census exact at every round, every named lock
  wait observed, three consecutive green runs **on the final code** (the Phase 11 gate's I1: runs on an
  earlier commit do not count), and its probes caught.
- **Idempotency**: exercised (duplicate keys, duplicate ticks, duplicate provider answers, lapsed claims).
- **Consistency**: exercised (every census in one snapshot, every round).
- **Atomicity**: exercised (the crash points; a forced failure at every T-pur step leaves nothing).
- **Failure handling**: exercised (lost payout and top-up responses, killed backends, restarts, a wallet not
  postable, capital exhausted).
- **Security**: the storm's actors hold only their roles and keys; no figure in its logs.
- **Audit**: every act counted against its audit rows, the refused ones `FAILED`.
- **Observability**: every gauge zero at rest; the sweepers' enabled gauges asserted; the meters' census
  over the whole run.
- **Reconciliation implications**: the censuses are the reconciliation; the merchant payouts' expectations

- **Tests**: `BnplStormDatabaseTest` (`:app:ownContainerDatabaseTest`).
- **Probe**: `PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §13.4's set, each on the whole storm, each caught by its census and recorded

  refund earliest-first; skip the purchase lock in a refund; pro-rate the fee by a running clamp; skip L6; read

  plus the storm's own — accrue inside T-svc after the wallet (the income-row census), take the payable and

- **Acceptance criteria**: three consecutive green runs on the final code; every probe caught; every
  scenario exercised; the hot-row measurement recorded.
- **Definition of done**: `DOD-TEST`, `DOD-FIN` (F1–F8 binding over the storm's postings; F5 — the
  duplicated provider answers and webhooks of both scenario 5 variants). **Risk**: High. **Cx**: XL.

**P12-TST-002 — The BNPL battery** — `PLANNED`
- **Objective**: exactness and replay over a large generated portfolio of both products — schedules, accrual,
  allocation, refunds and fee return — in two JVMs.
- **Bounded context**: BNPL (`creditmath`'s engines as bnpl pins them).
- **Dependencies**: `-008`, `-009`, `-021`, `-022`.
- **Scope**: `PHASE_12_PLAN.md` §13.3: ≥ 10,000 generated purchases across both products and every plan
  (P4; PN 3, 6, 12), amounts including non-divisible-by-4 and the product bounds' edges, PN rates including
  the terms' extremes, purchase dates across leap and non-leap years and month ends (over-sampled), random
  repayment (on time, late, partial, over), collection, refund (partial and full; before, during and after
  the instalments; after closure) and dispute sequences (a refund outcome as a refund, an upheld one as
  nothing) on a simulated calendar; written by **independent oracles**, never the production engines (the
  Phase 11 battery's Q2: without them the probes are invisible) and replayed through `BnplReplayer`; every
  figure replayed `IDENTICAL` in two JVMs; **value preservation** (`INV-BNPL-06`) for every refund and
  **fee telescoping** (Σ fee returned = `f` at a full refund, whatever the order and split) for every refund
  order; the P4 split conserving `P` exactly (A4) and every schedule conserving principal (`INV-BNPL-05`); a
  perturbed allocation, refund adjustment, accrual or agreement byte flips the verdict, each perturbation
  naming its row (the Phase 11 gate's `Flip.namesItsRow`); an engine version swapped under a stored number
  `DIVERGED`; selections by a mixed hash of the index, never the generator's walk (the same gate's second
  finding); coverage floors (leap days, month-end purchases, non-divisible amounts, refunds in each phase,
  closures by each reason); a population fingerprint committed; a probe-only size knob
  (`FINAPP_BNPL_BATTERY_PURCHASES`, the `FINAPP_LENDING_BATTERY_LOANS` precedent — a shrunk run fails the
  census by design).
- **Out of scope**: concurrency (the storm's); operator-resolved disputes as a separate path (their outcome
  is a refund); lending's battery (re-run `IDENTICAL` by `-002`).
- **Domain changes**: none — tests.

- **Idempotency**: N/A — pure.
- **Consistency**: N/A — pure.
- **Atomicity**: N/A — pure.
- **Failure handling**: every reason for divergence exercised by perturbation.
- **Security**: none.
- **Audit**: none.
- **Observability**: none.
